title: Pomoni on algoritmi – tekoäly tuli jo työpaikoille, lainsäädäntö laahaa perässä
content:
Euroopan unioni valmistelee uusia sääntöjä tekoälyn käytöstä työpaikoilla. Ay-liikkeen mukaan työntekijöiden digitaalinen valvonta on jo arkipäivää, mutta alan lainsäädäntö laahaa jäljessä.

SAK:N ja STTK:n yhteisen Brysselin-edunvalvontatoimiston FinUnionsin johtaja Susanna Salovaara pelkää, että poliittinen ilmapiiri vesittää vastedeskin Euroopan yhteiset sääntelyuudistukset asiassa.

Eurooppalaisilla työpaikoilla on käynnissä hiljainen vallankumous, jossa työntekijöiden arkeen vaikuttavaa päätösvaltaa siirtyy yhä enemmän tietojärjestelmille.

Työvuorojen jakaminen, työsuoritusten arviointi, rekrytointi ja jopa työntekijöiden tulevaisuutta koskevat ratkaisut voidaan perustaa algoritmien tuottamiin suosituksiin.

Työntekijä ei kuitenkaan välttämättä tiedä, millä perusteella häntä arvioidaan tai miten järjestelmän tekemään johtopäätökseen voisi vaikuttaa.

Pahimmillaan päätösten perusteita ei osaa selittää edes työntekijän esihenkilö.

KYSE EI ENÄÄ OLE tulevaisuuden uhkakuvasta, Susanna Salovaara varoittaa.

title: Dagaare Wikimedians Celebrate Wikidata’s 14th Birthday in Ghana
content:
We celebrated, learn, had interesting conversations, laughter, photography and of course, a delicious birthday cake! We also meet an active community member for the first time in person and some other community members who join the celebration and had an opportunity to learn more about Wikidata.

The Dagaare Wikimedia Community brought people together to celebrate free knowledge, learn about Wikimedia projects and enjoy the spirits of community.

On 29th of October 2026, Dagaare Wikimedians came together to celebrate Wikidata’s 14th birthday. It was a great opportunity to learn, share experiences, meet new people and celebrate the important role that Wikidata plays in making knowledge freely accessible to everyone.

title: Letter from a jailed Azerbaijani political prisoner reveals deadly consequences of silence
content:
The Trump administration’s blind eye to severe human rights violations in Azerbaijan is deadly for political prisoners

Originally published on Global Voices

Bahruz Samadov being brought to Sabail District Court in 2024. Image by Voice of America, via Wikimedia Commons. Public domain.

Bahruz Samadov is an Azerbaijani political scientist, peace activist, and PhD candidate at Charles University in Prague, or at least he was until the summer of 2024. On August 21, 2024, the State Security Service detained Samadov while he was visiting his grandmother in Baku. Global Voices reported on his arrest at the time, as part of a wider crackdown on critics before Azerbaijan hosted COP29 in November 2024.

title: Vuoden kieltenopettaja poistaa oppimisen esteitä
content:
Suomen kieltenopettajien liitto SUKOL ry on valinnut Vuoden kieltenopettajaksi Anna-Leena Haapalan, joka opettaa englantia ja ruotsia Saskyn Tampereen palvelualan ammattiopistossa. Työssään Haapala pitää tärkeänä sitä, että kaikki hänen opiskelijansa saavat peruskielitaidon ja rohkeutta puhua. Opiskelijan motivoiminen on keskeinen osa hänen opetustaan. ”Kun opiskelija rohkaistuu ja uskaltaa keskustella englanniksi tai ruotsiksi opettajan kuullen, on ainakin yksi este oppimisen tieltä ylitetty”, Haapala sanoo.

Haapalan työpaikka Tampereen palvelualan ammattiopisto on osa Sasky-koulutuskuntayhtymää, joka toimii usean kunnan alueella Pirkanmaalla ja Satakunnassa. Haapalalla on kokemusta muiltakin asteilta, mutta suurimman osan työurastaan hän on toiminut ammatillisella toisella asteella. Hänen mielestään ammatillisen kieltenopettajan työssä erityisen hienoa on opiskelijan kohtaaminen ja kannustaminen opiskelemaan ainetta, joka tuntuu vaikealta: ”Onnistumisen fiilis on molemminpuolinen ja mahtava silloin, kun joku oppii ääntämään oikein vaikean sanan tai muistaa kirjoittaa jonkin rakenteen oikein.”

title: I Investigated the Online Sports Betting Industry. DraftKings Shut Down My Account.
content:
Late last month, I was getting dinner on the table when an email hit my inbox with some bad news.

“Upon review your account has been closed at DraftKings’ discretion,” the message read. “We understand that this is not the decision that you were hoping for but this decision is final.” 

I hadn’t bet on sports in months and had withdrawn all but a few cents of my balance. Why, I wondered, would my account even be under review? Was it something I’d said?

In September, I’d published an investigation into how online sports betting companies like DraftKings court customers — and whether the internal guardrails they’ve put in place to stop their users from spiraling out of control are firm enough. For that piece, I’d intentionally bet like a problem gambler, recklessly escalating my betting behavior over 10 weeks. My wagering had been informed by a panel of professional sports bettors, recovering addicts and addiction specialists.

As I flagrantly waved the red flags, DraftKings made me a VIP and assigned me my very own personal host. My recklessness was being rewarded. It just took three weeks and about $6,000 of losses.

title: Årets språklärare undanröjer hinder för lärande
content:
Språklärarförbundet i Finland SUKOL rf har utsett Anna-Leena Haapala till Årets språklärare. Haapala undervisar i engelska och svenska vid Sasky Tammerfors yrkesinstitut för servicebranschen. Det är viktigt för henne att alla hennes studerande får grundläggande språkkunskaper och mod att tala. Att motivera den studerande är en central del av hennes undervisning. “När den studerande får mod och vågar samtala på engelska eller svenska i lärarens närvaro, har man åtminstone övervunnit ett hinder för lärandet”, säger hon.

Tammerfors yrkesinstitut för servicebranschen är en del av utbildningssamkommunen Sasky, som verkar inom flera kommuners område i Birkaland och Satakunta. Anna-Leena Haapala har erfarenhet även från andra stadier, men största delen av sin yrkeskarriär har hon arbetat inom yrkesutbildningen på andra stadiet. Det som enligt henne är särskilt fint i yrkeslärarens arbete är mötet med de studerande och att uppmuntra dem att studera ett ämne som känns svårt: ”Känslan av framgång är ömsesidig och fantastisk när någon lär sig uttala ett svårt ord rätt eller kommer ihåg att skriva en struktur korrekt.”

title: Suzanne Innes-Stubb kannustaa puhumaan eri kieliä virheitä pelkäämättä
content:
Suomen kieltenopettajien liitto SUKOL ry myöntää Vuoden kieliteko 2026 -palkinnon Suzanne Innes-Stubbille. Vuoden kieliteko -palkinto jaetaan vuosittain toiminnasta, joka on edistänyt monikielisyyttä tai lisännyt kieltenopetuksen yhteiskunnallista arvostusta.

Tasavallan presidentin puolison roolissa Innes-Stubbin esimerkillä on laajaa vaikutusta. Hän ei ole tyytynyt käyttämään pelkästään äidinkieltään englantia, vaikka sillä tulisikin toimeen. Muun kielitaitonsa lisäksi hän on opetellut suomen ja ruotsin kieltä ja puhuu molempia kansalliskieliä sujuvasti. Kansallisten kielten osaaminen on hänen kohdallaan ollut myös tie suomalaisten sydämiin.

Innes-Stubb on opiskellut oikeustiedettä sekä ranskaa ja saksaa ja toiminut työurallaan kansainvälisissä tehtävissä muun muassa kilpailulainsäädännön parissa. Perheensä monikielisyyttä hän kuvailee seuraavasti: ”Puhun englantia lapsillemme, mieheni puhuu heille ruotsia, muut perheenjäsenet puhuvat suomea, ja meillä on hyviä ystäviä, jotka puhuvat ranskaa.” Innes-Stubb onkin erinomainen esimerkki kielitaidon tärkeästä roolista niin arjessa kuin vaativissa kansainvälisissä suhteissa.

title: Suzanne Innes-Stubb uppmuntrar till att tala olika språk utan rädsla för misstag
content:
Språklärarförbundet i Finland SUKOL rf tilldelar Suzanne Innes-Stubb priset Årets språkgärning 2026. Priset Årets språkgärning delas ut årligen för verksamhet som har främjat flerspråkigheten eller höjt språkundervisningens samhälleliga status.

I rollen som republikens presidents maka har Innes-Stubbs exempel en bred inverkan. Hon har inte nöjt sig med att använda enbart sitt modersmål engelska, även om hon skulle klara sig med det. Vid sidan av sina övriga språkkunskaper har hon lärt sig finska och svenska och talar båda nationalspråken flytande. Kunskaperna i de nationella språken har för hennes del också varit en väg till finländarnas hjärtan.

Innes-Stubb har studerat juridik samt franska och tyska och har under sin karriär arbetat i internationella uppgifter bland annat med konkurrenslagstiftning. Familjens flerspråkighet beskriver hon så här: ”Jag talar engelska med våra barn, min man talar svenska med dem, övriga familjemedlemmar talar finska, och vi har goda vänner som talar franska.” Innes-Stubb är ett utmärkt exempel på språkkunskapens viktiga roll både i vardagen och i krävande internationella relationer.

title: Lawfare Daily: Aya Ibrahim on Progressive Priorities for the New Democratic Congress
content:
In this episode of the Security Economics podcast series, Peter Harrell and AI Now’s Aya Ibrahim discuss the agenda for the next Congress, AI regulation, and U.S.-China policy.

Aya joins Lawfare Contributing Editor and host of the Security Economics podcast Peter Harrell to talk about a progressive agenda for the next Congress, about AI regulation, and about U.S.-China policy. Aya and Peter also look back at things that the Biden Administration got right—and wrong—about U.S.-China competition, and they close by talking about how to balance security economics with the domestic economy. 

This episode is part of the Security Economics podcast series, in which Peter Harrell and guests explore the intersection of economics and national security, how countries manage their economies to support national security, and how they deploy economic tools in support of geopolitical objectives.

Comma is an international, multilingual journal covering the professional administration and development of archives and archivists worldwide. It aims to reach the widest possible global readership.

Comma usually publishes two themed issues per year. Its content includes contributions from ICA Congresses and Conferences, reports and studies based on the work of ICA Regional Branches, Professional Sections and Expert Groups, and special thematic issues. title: Russia’s Security State Will Not Abandon Dark Arts
content:
There is much talk about peace in Ukraine as US-brokered talks continue, and much skepticism. But if Vladimir Putin does sign a deal, there is one rarely voiced but critical question worth asking: how will Russian intelligence agencies respond?  

The answer? It would taste like poison to the Russian security state. At the very least, it would refuse to stop increasingly aggressive shadow war operations abroad. A pause is possible, but renunciation of the sabotage, political assassination, and other dark arts is unimaginable. 

How do we know? Look at recent history. 

When the KGB-orchestrated coup d’état failed in Moscow in August 1991, leading to the swift collapse of the Soviet Union, Russian President Boris Yeltsin appeared fully committed to reforming the KGB. He went as far as splitting a monstrous, all-encompassing organization into several agencies.  

But the division responsible for its offensive capabilities proved the most resistant to change, and the most resourceful.

title: Young people’s wellbeing is essential for meaningful participation in peacebuilding
content:
At the Stockholm Forum, a session organised by CMI and Search for Common Ground explored how mental health and psychosocial support can help young people engage in civic life and peacebuilding processes. Drawing on experiences from Mali, Palestine, and Ukraine, participants shared insights on how psychosocial support can be better integrated into peacebuilding efforts.

Young people in conflict-affected settings are often portrayed as victims, risks, or symbols of resilience. Such narratives overlook the profound psychosocial impacts of violence, displacement, and prolonged insecurity, and the ways these experiences shape young people’s participation in peacebuilding and civic life.

Today, an estimated one in four young people live in contexts affected by conflict, and many experience mental health and psychosocial distress. In countries such as Mali, Palestine, and Ukraine, young people navigate not only immediate crisis, but also the lasting effects of intergenerational trauma, social fragmentation, and mistrust. Yet peacebuilding efforts rarely address these realities in a systematic way.

title: Science in a Complex World: Why Our Future Depends on More Than Scientific Discovery
content:
Reflections from the Beijing Science Dialogue and International Science Council Midterm Meeting, Beijing, China | 19–23 October 2026

By Ntsundeni Louis Mapatagane (CODATA)

Ntsundeni Louis Mapatagena is Co-chair of CODATA Connect, CODATA’s Early Career Network, Director of Planning and Institutional Intelligence at Walter Sisulu University (WSU), MSc Environmental Sciences, Ph.D Candidate on the readiness of higher education institutions for energy efficiency and emissions reduction.

I travelled to Beijing, China, for the Beijing Science Dialogue and International Science Council (ISC) Midterm Meeting, expecting to engage in conversations about the future of science, international scientific cooperation and the opportunities and challenges presented by emerging technologies. I returned with something more profound: a renewed appreciation that the greatest challenge facing science may not necessarily be our ability to generate knowledge, but our collective ability to translate that knowledge into trust, responsible behaviour, effective policy and meaningful societal change.

title: Janne Riiheläinen: Miksi infopuolustuksen kehitys vesittyi näin pahasti?
content:
Hallitus lupasi tehdä vieraan valtion informaatiokätyrinä toimimisesta rangaistavaa – erilaisten Kremlin kellokkaiden työn vaikeuttamiseksi. Silti jostain mystisistä syistä tämä ja monet muutkin puolustushankkeet vesittyivät.

Ensin kehut: vastikään ilmestyneessä uudessa Kansallisessa riskiarviossa informaatiovaikuttaminen on näkyvästi mukana.

Saman uhkakuvan ovat jakaneet kaikki viime vuosien keskeiset valtiolliset asiakirjat ja selonteot, joissa aihetta on käsitelty.

Päättäjillä ja virkamieskunnassa vallitsee näiden perusteella ymmärrys siitä, miten vihamielisten valtioiden meihin kohdistama informaatiovaikuttaminen on yhdenlaista kognitiivista sodankäyntiä.

Uhan torjunnan ajatellaan vaativan perinteisempien puolustustoimien rinnalle uusia konsteja, sekä koko yhteiskunnan läpäisevää henkistä kriisinkestävyyttä ja kriittistä medialukutaitoa.

UUDESSA riskiarviossa on analysoitu myös infovaikuttajien keinoja ja tekniikkaa ansiokkaasti.

Keskeinen huomio on, että fyysisen maailman konkreettisilla teoilla vihollinen saa usein huomattavasti vaikuttavampia ja pitkäkestoisempia reaktioita informaatiokenttäänkin kun pelkällä ”trollaamisella” tai propagandan jaolla.

title: Connecting authors of Basque documentary heritage on Wikipedia and Wikidata
content:
The programme “Connecting authors of Basque documentary heritage on Wikipedia and Wikidata”, launched by the Sancho el Sabio Vital Foundation and Wikimedia Spain, has promoted the dissemination of Basque documentary heritage through free knowledge, combining training, guidance and collaborative editing. 

Over the course of several months, the initiative has introduced Wikimedia tools to professionals and new audiences, with the aim of raising the profile of authors linked to Basque culture. 

In total, 43 people took part in the programme’s activities, which unfolded in different stages, from the initial training sessions to an edit-a-thon dedicated to putting the knowledge gained into practice. 

The various sessions featured Wikimedia Spain members with experience of the Wikimedia ecosystem and specialist knowledge of its projects and tools. Their contribution enabled the programme to cover everything from the principles of editing on Wikipedia to the potential of Wikidata for cultural institutions, combining technical knowledge and practical experience.

title: AI and bots on the campaign trail: What Poland can learn from Hungary
content:
On screen, a young Hungarian soldier stands on the Ukrainian front line. Moments later, he is killed, leaving a child crying at home. The scene looks like something from a war movie. But it was generated using artificial intelligence.

The video was published in February 2026 by the Budapest branch of Fidesz, Viktor Orbán’s party. Its message was clear: a victory for Péter Magyar’s opposition Tisza party could drag Hungary into war.

It was hardly an isolated incident. Ahead of the April 12, 2026, parliamentary election, artificial intelligence became one of the principal weapons in the political battle. Videos, images and other material were generated to attack opponents. They spread not only through official party accounts but also through affiliated organizations, influencers and networks of social media accounts.

“Using AI in political campaigns was not new. What was new during this election campaign was that they used it massively,” says Zsófia Fülöp, a journalist at the Hungarian fact-checking outlet Lakmusz who investigated disinformation during this year’s parliamentary election.

title: The grand art-taking - Tracking Europe's missing paintings
content: Over the past century, art thieves have stolen 27 Van Gogh masterpieces across Europe, more than any other famous artist by a healthy margin. But if you add up mainstream cinema hits, TV series, and even docu-dramas, the favourite victim is Rembrandt, followed by Degas and Rubens. Van Gogh’s lead owes a lot to one very ambitious night. On 14 April 1991, 20 paintings vanished from Amsterdam’s Van Gogh Museum. Two armed men had hidden inside the building and, as it turned out, had help from within. Yet the world-famous Dutch painter remains underrepresented on screen, appearing in just two action films: The Train and the less-known Righteous Thieves, both involving Nazi art plundered during World War II. As for locations, both real-life and fictional art theft love glamorous capitals like Paris and London. Where the film industry exaggerates is the method: forged copies, disguises, and acrobatic roof-suspension instead of nighttime break-ins and improvised ladders. In films, masterpieces usually end up back on the wall. In reality, some never make it home. Caravaggio's Nativity was cut from its frame in Palermo in 1969 and has presumably been destroyed by the Mafia. Monet's Waterloo

Finland and Northern European Security research programme

The regional focus of the programme is Finland’s immediate security environment, developments in which have direct implications for Finland’s national security. The programme broadly monitors various aspects of Finland’s foreign, security, and defence policy, including Finland’s relations with major powers, its military cooperation, NATO’s activities, and the development of NATO’s defence and deterrence posture (including nuclear deterrence), Nordic cooperation, and Russia’s foreign, security, and defence policy in relation to Finland. title: Fingo: Olemme ottaneet yhteyttä oikeuskansleriin
content:
Kun virkahenkilöt arvioivat julkisesti ministerin toimineen lainvastaisesti, hallituskumppanit eivät voi mennä sen taakse, että tapaus kuuluu ministerin toimivaltaan.

Jaa

Fingo on pyytänyt oikeuskansleria tarkastelemaan ulkomaankauppa- ja kehitysministeri Ville Tavion (ps.) Somalia-päätöksen lainmukaisuutta. Fingo sai toimenpidepyyntöä varten sisältöä jäsenistöltään.

Tavio linjasi maanantaina sosiaalisen median kanavissaan, että hän ei tule myöntämään hanketukea järjestöjen Somaliaan suunnitelluille hankkeille – asiaa ei oltu ilmoitettu hakukriteereissä.

Fingo pyytää oikeuskansleria arvioimaan, onko tapauksessa aihetta laillisuusvalvonnallisiin toimenpiteisiin. Fingo näkee yhteydenottonsa toimenpidepyynnöksi, ei vielä viralliseksi kanteluksi.

Virallisia päätöksiä hanketuesta ei ole vielä tehty. Fingon tietojen mukaan ne on tarkoitus tehdä ensi viikolla.

Fingo on avannut aikaisemmassa tiedotteessaan kantaansa siitä, miksi Tavion toimintatapa on huonoa hallintoa.

title: Rechte Kaderschmiede: AfD-nahe Stiftung dürfte kein Geld bekommen
content:
Das Innenministerium prüft derzeit, ob die Desiderius-Erasmus-Stiftung mit Millionen Euro gefördert wird. Ihr müssen staatliche Mittel verwehrt bleiben.

Seit Jahren arbeitet sie darauf hin, bald könnte es soweit sein: Die AfD-nahe Desiderius-Erasmus-Stiftung (DES) möchte sich am Bundeshaushalt bedienen. Wenn es nach ihr geht, könnte sie bald Dutzende Millionen Euro staatliche Förderung erhalten. Doch ob die DES tatsächlich gefördert wird, prüft derzeit das Bundesinnenministerium von Alexander Dobrindt (CSU).

Um Geld aus der Staatskasse zu erhalten, müssen parteinahe Stiftungen gewährleisten, dass sie aktiv „für die freiheitliche demokratische Grundordnung sowie für den Gedanken der Völkerverständigung“ eintreten. Das verlangt seit 2024 das Stiftungsfinanzierungsgesetz. Bei der DES gibt es zahlreiche Aspekte, die gegen diese Voraussetzung sprechen. Deshalb müsste ihr die staatliche Förderung verwehrt bleiben. 

Dass die parteinahe Stiftung der extrem rechten AfD nicht für die freiheitliche demokratische Grundordnung eintritt, mag offensichtlich sein – jedoch muss das Innenministerium dies auch nachweisen, um der DES staatliche Unterstützung zu verweigern.

title: Georgia Fort stands up for journalists
content:
Independent journalist Georgia Fort is stepping up to call attention to retaliation against reporters, including her own ongoing prosecution for covering a protest at a Minnesota church against violence by immigration enforcement officers. Plus, some advice for the next Congress to fix the broken federal transparency system.

Georgia Fort is being prosecuted in a legally dubious case for her coverage of a protest against immigration authorities at a Minnesota church in January. She’s also been the subject of secret subpoenas. Unfortunately, while the scale of the government’s campaign against her is absurd, it’s not unprecedented — across the country, journalists are facing threats, arrests, and violence for keeping the public informed.

Now, Fort is partnering with the U.S. Press Freedom Tracker, a project of Freedom of the Press Foundation (FPF), as well as the Committee to Protect Journalists and Protect Democracy, on a video series highlighting the experiences of other journalists under attack and how the public’s right to know has been impacted.

title: Forskning i nord, regnskog i sør og propaganda i vår tid – Tildelinger til journalistikk høsten 2026
content:
Kaldt ytringsklima i nord, regnskogsbistand i Colombia og 10 forsøk om propaganda som er vanskelig å få øye på. Se de nye journalistikkprosjektene som fikk støtte høsten 2026.

På få år har nordområdene for alvor blitt en del av stormaktsspillet. NATO har styrket sitt nærvær i Arktis, Donald Trump har sagt at både Canada og Grønland bør innlemmes i USA, og Russland og Kina har markert sine strategiske interesser i regionen.

Hvordan preger dette kunnskapen vår om nordområdene? Det spør akademia-avisen Khrono seg i en serie som går gjennom 2027. Avisen har fått støtte til å undersøke hva den sikkerhetspolitiske situasjonen har å si for forskerne: hva de forsker på, hvem de samarbeider med, og hva de kan og tør å si offentlig.

– Dette er ikke et prosjekt om akademia for akademia, men noe bredere. Prosjektet handler om hvilken kunnskap som når den norske offentligheten i en situasjon der sikkerhetspolitiske hensyn får stadig større betydning.

title: Diamond Open Access for Scholarly Books: Lessons from Croatia
content:
Blog post by Iva Melinščak Zlodi (*)

The possibilities for making research openly accessible, and for enabling authors to retain control over their rights, are closely connected to the scholarly publishing models that dominate in different countries. This connection matters most in countries where resources to cover article and book processing charges (APCs and BPCs) are limited, and where publishing agreements that cover Open Access (OA) fees offer only partial solutions. Croatia offers a useful example of how established non-commercial publishing traditions can support more equitable access to scholarly knowledge.

title: Afgaaninaisen katse: “Olet muslimimies, mutta käytät tuollaisia lapsellisia vaatteita” – Taliban valvoo myös miesten pukeutumista
content:
Taliban valvoo jatkuvasti afganistanilaisten nuorten elämän pienimpiäkin yksityiskohtia. Mikä tahansa vaatekappale tai persoonallisen tyylin merkki voi johtaa kuulusteluihin ja rangaistuksiin Talibanin sääntöjen vastaisena. Matkapuhelinten tarkastuksista on tullut jokapäiväistä.

Rajoitukset koskevat etenkin naisia, mutta myös miesten elämänpiiristä on tullut näkymätön häkki. Jatkuva pelko on korvannut tulevaisuushaaveet. Painostus ja tarkkailu ovat lisänneet nuorten ahdistusta ja masennusta.

Neljä nuorta miestä kertoo nyt kokemuksistaan Kabulissa.

Farid (nimi muutettu), 27, asuu Khushhal Khanin alueella Kabulissa. Hän opiskeli yliopistossa taloustieteitä ja meni valmistuttuaan töihin yksityiseen firmaan.

Farid huokaisee muistellessaan esimerkkejä siitä, miten Talibanin moraalipoliisi on kohdellut häntä viiden viime vuoden aikana.

”Menin ruokakauppaan päälläni t-paita ja housut eli yksinkertaiset, tavalliset vaatteet. Käytän niitä usein, samoin kuin perahan tunbania (afganistanilainen perinteinen löysä asu). Vartaloni oli muuten peitossa, mutta t-paidassa oli lyhyet hihat.”

Kadulla Talibanin moraalipoliisit pysäyttivät Faridin ja alkoivat haukkua häntä.

title: Public Value and the BBC
content:
The BBC is under constant pressure to prove its value, and, like many other public institutions, it is viewed through a market-failure lens that limits its role to addressing gaps left by the private sector. It is also measured and evaluated by static, price-focused metrics that fail to capture outcomes that accumulate over time. That pressure is now coming to a head. Before the end of the year, the government will publish its White Paper on the BBC Charter Review, setting out its decisions on how the BBC will be funded, what its mission should be and which public purposes it should serve from 2028. How the BBC’s value is defined and measured will sit at the heart of those decisions.

Subscribe now

The Director-General of the BBC, Matt Brittin has the opportunity to re-shape and re-open the conversation surrounding value creation at the BBC. However, this conversation needs to start in the right way. That requires policymakers and regulators to recognise the BBC’s contribution to the British media landscape.

title: The Anatomy of “Harm”: An Interview with IFRRO CEO Anita Huss-Ekerhult on AI and Copyright
content:
Across different creative sectors, existing studies point to measurable and, in some cases, already quantified economic and commercial harm. At the same time, a market for AI licensing is already an established and growing commercial reality and this is continually undermined by unauthorized use.

title: Could you survive without Microsoft? Inside the costs of digital dependence
content:
When I arrived at work to discover that Outlook had vanished from my computer, I wondered how I was supposed to get through my working day. No emails. No calendar. No meeting invitations.

Then another thought crossed my mind: when did we become so dependent on a single technology company that losing access to one application could disrupt our entire working routine? And what is the financial and environmental cost of that dependence?

We regularly discuss sustainability in terms of reducing plastic, cutting carbon emissions and consuming less energy. But the digital systems we rely on every day also have huge environmental consequences.

As world leaders gather at the UN climate summit, Cop31, in Turkey, perhaps it is time to ask an uncomfortable question: can our digital economy really become sustainable when so much of it depends on a handful of technology companies?

The cloud may sound weightless, but it runs on data centres, electricity, cooling systems and hardware.

title: Maria da Penha -laki täytti 20 vuotta, mutta Brasilian naiset eivät vieläkään ole turvassa
content:
Brasilia on vahvistanut naisiin kohdistuvaa väkivaltaa torjuvaa lainsäädäntöään jo kahden vuosikymmenen ajan. Silti tuhannet naiset joutuvat vuosittain lähisuhdeväkivallan uhreiksi. Ongelma ei kuitenkaan välttämättä ole lain puutteissa, vaan yhteiskunnallisissa asenteissa ja viranomaisten kyvyssä taata naisille todellista turvallisuutta.

Toukokuussa vuonna 1983 brasilialainen farmaseutti Maria da Penha Maia Fernandes oli nukkumassa kotonaan, kun hän heräsi yhtäkkiä kovaan pamaukseen ja voimakkaaseen kipuun selässään. Marian mies, joka oli ollut väkivaltainen häntä ja heidän yhteisiä lapsiaan kohtaan jo aiemmin, oli yrittänyt tappaa Marian ampumalla häntä selkään. Maria halvaantui hyökkäyksessä, joka ei jäänyt viimeiseksi laatuaan, vaan mies yritti tappaa hänet myöhemmin vielä uudestaan samana vuonna sähköiskulla Marian ollessa kylvyssä. Maria selvisi hengissä molemmista hyökkäyksistä ja on tämän jälkeen omistanut elämänsä taistelulle naisten oikeuksien puolesta.

title: What’s the difference between being not racist and being anti-racist?
content:
There is a big difference between being not racist and anti-racist.

Perhaps you can recall a time when you heard someone saying something racist, or acting racist. Non-racist people don’t want to rock the boat. They wouldn’t confront the antagonizer. Rather than saying what they think, they would stay silent and maybe talk about what happened after.

Anti-racists look around and think about what they can do, what tools they have, or what they can say to make it clear that racist behaviour is unacceptable. That doesn’t mean they are rude to people but that they will call people out in a polite way when they hear racist language or see racist behaviour.

Being anti-racist also means looking beyond individual behaviour. Anti-racists look at the roots of systemic racism in power, policies, institutions and histories, and see how they can produce or sustain racial hierarchies and inequalities.

This means that being not racist is about what you don’t do and being anti-racist is about how do you understand, acknowledge, challenge and take action to change unequal systems that produce racial inequality.

title: Tech Companies Are Trying to Shift the Entire Concept of Privacy (Again)
content:
Privacy, which companies were once happy to claim was all about personal choice, is now primed to affect everyone around you even more than it already did.

Meta and Google’s smart glasses can record anything the owner is looking at or use artificial intelligence to describe it. Apple’s* Audio Intelligence feature turns every Apple Watch into a transcription machine that records or summarizes your day. Amazon’s Bee devices take that a step further and can record and transcribe everything. Dozens of other companies are introducing pendants, rings, and other products designed to record, transcribe, or summarize everything we say and do all day long.

Privacy has always been a team sport. The actions you take with communication apps, collaborative software, or your cloud backup solutions, have long impacted everyone else you’re interacting with. But moving those choices deeper into the physical world where strangers, colleagues, family, and friends are all now a part of your privacy choices is drastically changing the game.
snippet: Privacy, which companies were once happy to claim was all about personal choice, is now primed to affect everyone around you even more than it already did.

title: Three Members of Bushehr Teachers’ Trade Association Sentenced to Prison and Additional Penalties
content:
According to HRANA, citing the Coordinating Council of Iranian Teachers’ Trade Associations, three teachers’ union activists in Bushehr Province have been sentenced to imprisonment and additional penalties.

According to the report, a judicial authority sentenced Reza (Abdolreza) Amanifar, Asghar Hajeb, and Roghayeh Torabpour to prison terms and additional penalties on charges of “collaboration in political, cultural, and propaganda activities against national security.”

Under the verdict, Amanifar was sentenced to 10 years and one day in prison, Hajeb to two years in prison, and Torabpour to six months in prison, with time already served in detention credited toward her sentence. As additional penalties, each of the three was also sentenced to permanent dismissal from government and public service positions and confiscation of their electronic devices.

The report did not provide further details, including the date the verdict was issued or the judicial authority responsible for issuing it.

In September of this year, Reza (Abdolreza) Amanifar and Asghar Hajeb were summoned to court in separate cases.

content:
Suomi-Seura ry on valinnut Vuoden ulkosuomalaiseksi 2026 suomalaissaksalaisen Uusikuu-yhtyeen, joka viettää tänä vuonna 20-vuotisjuhlavuottaan. Uusikuu on vaalinut suomalaista musiikkiperinnettä, luonut ulkosuomalaisille kohtaamisia ja tehnyt suomen kieltä ja suomalaista kulttuuria tunnetuksi erityisesti Euroopassa. title: Kasvuyritysten rahoituksen saatavuutta tulee parantaa
content:
Erityisesti nuoret, aineettomiin investointeihin nojaavat yritykset tarvitsevat sijoittajia, joilla on riittävästi pääomaa ja kykyä rahoittaa yrityksiä useiden tappiollisten vuosien ajan. Tämä käy ilmi eduskunnan tarkastusvaliokunnan tilaamasta Etla-tutkimuksesta, jossa tarkastellaan yritysrahoituksen saatavuutta ja toteutunutta käyttöä. Tutkimuksessa ehdotetaan myös, että kasvuun tähtäävien julkisten avustusten nykyistä vahvempaa kohdentamista mikro- ja pienyrityksiin tulee kokeilla ja arvioida sen vaikutuksia.

Suomalaiset yritykset rahoittavat toimintaansa ennen kaikkea omilla voitoillaan ja pankkilainalla. Muita keskeisiä rahoitusmuotoja ovat omistajien tekemät pääomasijoitukset ja erilainen julkinen rahoitus kuten avustukset, lainat, takaukset ja verotuet.

Vuonna 2023 kertyneet voittovarat kasvoivat runsaalla puolella yrityksistä. Pankkilainaa oli noin 32 prosentilla yrityksistä. Pankkilainan käyttö oli yleisintä 6–10 vuotta toimineissa yrityksissä. Rahoituksen käyttö vaihteli kuitenkin enemmän yrityksen koon kuin iän mukaan.

Eri rahoitusmuotojen yhteiskäyttö oli yrityksissä melko vähäistä, sanoo Etlan tutkimusjohtaja Heli Koski.

title: Essee: Mikä oli se raja, johon illiberaalin populismin nousu tänä vuonna törmäsi?
content:
Orbán menetti vallan Unkarissa, Serbian opiskelijat voittivat ja demokraatit ottivat vallan Yhdysvaltojen kongressissa – ja demokratian luisu pysähtyi näissä maissa ainakin toistaiseksi. Yritykset rakentaa illiberaalia tiedon infrastruktuuria kaatuivat lopulta hallintojen omiin virheisiin, jotka osoittautuivat kestämättömän suuriksi, väittää Eurooppalaisen Suomen erityisasiantuntija Samuel Tammekann. Mutta riittääkö se pelastamaan demokratian?

Illiberaalin populismin voittokulku on ollut itsestäänselväksi muodostunut synkkä suuri kertomus 2020-luvun ihmiselle. Kysymys ei ole enää ollut, mikä on demokratiakehityksen suunta, vaan milloin ja missä seuraava taantuminen tapahtuu. 

Raporttimme alkuperäinen, Trumpin toisen kauden alun varjostama tutkimuskysymys kuului seuraavasti: miten EU voi puolustaa arvopohjaista järjestelmää ja demokratiaa maailman murroksessa? Kysymys lähti oletuksesta Yhdysvaltojen strategisesta vetäytymisestä ja uusien puolustuslinjojen rakentamisesta ”viimeiselle liberaalidemokraattiselle suurvallalle” hyvin uudenlaisessa ajassa.

content:

Palkinto on merkittävä kansainvälinen tunnustus kampanjalle, jonka tavoitteena on ollut herättää keskustelua musiikin arvosta aikana, jolloin musiikin kulutustavat muuttuvat nopeasti ja tekoäly haastaa luovan työn merkitystä.

Kampanjan viesti tavoitti miljoonia suomalaisia ja nosti esiin kysymyksen siitä, mistä musiikin todellinen arvo syntyy.

Kansainvälinen palkinto jatkaa kampanjan menestyksekästä vuotta. title: Anne Juppo appointed Guest Professor at the University of Copenhagen
content:
The appointment is supported by the NordForsk-funded NordicPharmaTrain project, which promotes Nordic collaboration in pharmaceutical research, new joint projects and innovation.

The guest professorship is a 20% part-time position, and Juppo will continue in her professorship at the University of Helsinki for the remaining 80%.

In Copenhagen, Juppo will develop research collaboration between Industrial Pharmacy at the University of Helsinki and the Department of Pharmacy in Copenhagen. She will also initiate and strengthen partnerships with the pharmaceutical industry, particularly in the Medicon Valley region.

In addition, Juppo will contribute to the revision of the industrial pharmacy elements of the University of Copenhagen curriculum and supervise doctoral researchers and postdoctoral researchers. The aim is also to plan joint research on preparedness and resilience in the health care sector and to pursue joint funding opportunities.

title: Israel Bans Travel for Prominent Palestinian Rights Defender
content:
(Beirut) – Israeli authorities on November 13, 2026, imposed an international travel ban on Shawan Jabarin, the head of Al-Haq, a leading Palestinian human rights organization in the occupied West Bank. The travel ban comes in the context of increasing attacks against Palestinians and civil society groups in the Occupied Palestinian Territory. 

Al-Haq, along with the Palestinian Centre for Human Rights and Al-Mezan Center for Human Rights, are continuing their critical human rights work despite US sanctions for engaging with the International Criminal Court. Human Rights Watch, with three other human rights organizations, filed a lawsuit in US federal court on August 11 seeking to have the sanctions struck down.

title: Emilia Palonen on Vuoden tieteentekijä 2026
content:
Emilia Palonen työskentelee valtio-opin apulaisprofessorina ja datafikaation ohjelmajohtajana Helsingin yliopiston valtiotieteellisessä tiedekunnassa.

- Emilia Palosen ansiot eivät rajoitu omiin tieteellisiin meriitteihin, vaan hän on kantanut tutkimustyönsä rinnalla laajasti vastuuta tieteellisissä seuroissa, järjestöissä ja luottamustehtävissä. Tällainen korvaamattoman tärkeä työ jää usein piiloon, vaikka ilman sitä tiedeyhteisö ei toimisi, Tieteentekijöiden puheenjohtaja Antti Pajala sanoo.

Palosen panos on ollut erityisen merkittävä avoimen tieteen ja avoimen julkaisemisen kehittämisessä. Tieteellisten seurain valtuuskunnassa sekä avoimen tieteen kansallisessa koordinaatiossa hän on ollut rakentamassa käytäntöjä, jotka parantavat tutkimuksen läpinäkyvyyttä, saavutettavuutta ja yhteiskunnallista vaikuttavuutta. Hän on ollut mukana myös kehittämässä tutkimustiedon infrastruktuureja ja tiedon saatavuutta tukevaa yhteistyötä, joka hyödyttää koko tiedeyhteisöä.

title: Tilastokeskus korjasi tammi–syyskuun asuntomarkkinalukuja – lokakuussa tehtiin yli 3 000 digitaalista asuntokauppaa
content:
Digitaalisten DIAS-kauppojen osuus kaikista kiinteistönvälittäjien tekemistä vanhojen asunto-osakkeiden kaupoista on kasvanut tänä vuonna aiemmin raportoitua hitaammin, kun asuntokauppoja on solmittu tammi–syyskuussa yhdeksän prosenttia luultua enemmän. Tilastokeskuksen 10.11. korjaamien kauppalukujen perusteella 60 prosenttia tänä aikana välitetyistä vanhojen asunto-osakkeiden kaupoista tehtiin DIAS-kauppoina.

Oikaistut luvut muuttavat myös DIASin aiemmin ilmoittamia yksittäisten kuukausien markkinaosuuksia. Heinäkuu säilyy edelleen DIAS-kaupan ennätyskuukautena, mutta aiemmin ilmoitetun 73 prosentin sijaan 66 prosenttia välittäjien kuun aikana tekemistä asunto-osakekaupoista solmittiin DIAS-alustalla.

Välittäjien tekemien asunto-osakekauppojen määrä oikaistuissa tilastoissa kasvoi eniten – lähes 15 prosenttia – syyskuussa. DIAS-kauppojen osuus kaikista välittäjien tekemistä vanhojen asunto-osakkeiden kaupoista syyskuussa oli siten mediatiedotteessa kerrotun 71 prosentin sijaan 62 prosenttia. Syyskuussa 2025 vastaava luku oli 57 prosenttia.

title: Serbia’s Experiment: Combining Democracy & Meritocracy
content:
It is no less true for being a cliché that innovation comes mostly from the edges. Whether in politics, markets or technology, fresh approaches emerge from the periphery and the margins rather than the well-established core. When it comes to the governing practices and institutions of democracies, innovation tends also to arrive not from the mature states, but the fledgling ones, less bound by legacy structures and entrenched constituencies.

That is the case today in Serbia, which only became a sovereign state in its own right in 2006 after its split from Montenegro following the breakup of Cold War-era Yugoslavia that began unraveling in 1992.

For the last 14 years, it has been ruled by a corrupt autocrat, Aleksandr Vučić, in the mold of Hungary’s Viktor Orbán. When his regime became too much to bear, a revolt by the nation’s youth erupted. The straw that broke the camel’s back came in November 2024 when the concrete canopy of a train station in Novi Sad collapsed and killed 16 people. Its shoddy construction was blamed on corruption in building permits and lax oversight inspections.

title: Five Questions About the Future of Global Anticorruption Efforts in the Trump Era
content:
After winning control of the United States Congress and Senate in midterm elections this month, the Democratic Party is expected to mount a firmer resistance to the dismantling of anti-corruption laws, institutions, and norms that has taken place under the Republican administration of President Donald Trump.

As part of Trump’s “America First” approach to foreign policy, the U.S. has narrowed enforcement of the Foreign Corrupt Practices Act (FCPA), the law designed to prohibit U.S. citizens or companies from bribing foreign officials for business, officially withdrawn from GRECO, the Council of Europe’s anti-corruption body, and gutted the U.S. Corporate Transparency Act, a 2020 law aimed at combating money laundering and illicit finance.

Kevin E. Davis, Beller Family Professor of Business Law at the New York University School of Law, discusses these changes and which foreign powers may fill the void that Trump’s administration has left in prosecuting transnational corruption.

title: When Animals Were Put on Trial in Medieval Europe
content: Most of us twenty-first-century urbanites have a fairly sentimental view of farm animals, precisely because so many generations have gone by since they’ve been part of our daily lives. (In South Korea, where I live, the agricultural past remains just within living memory. Perhaps that’s why so many restaurants in Seoul advertise their meat with pictures of the animals it comes from, sometimes dressed in chef’s garb and cheerfully serving up the very dishes they’re about to become.) Things were different in medieval Europe, where animals were both a necessity and a potential danger. History records many instances of serious harm done to humans by horses, bulls, and especially pigs, who seem to have had a particular tendency to turn on children.

title: EU deal on Ukraine talks overshadows AI-focused summit in Dublin
content:
They came to discuss AI, but EU leaders spent most of their time during a summit in Dublin on Friday grappling with questions about Ukraine — namely who should represent them in future peace talks.

Despite plenty of disagreement about whether it should be a single person (and if so, who) or a collection of them, they managed to strike a deal: Future talks would involve national security officials from Germany, France, the U.K., Italy and Poland — the so-called E5 powers — plus representatives from the European Commission and European Council. A classic European compromise.

“It is essential to have a team and to speak with one voice,” European Council President António Costa said after the summit, noting that Donald Trump had also tasked two envoys, Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner, with conducting negotiations.

Ireland, which holds the EU’s rotating presidency and hosted the informal gathering, had billed the meeting as a rare chance for a high-level discussion on how to develop artificial intelligence in accordance with European values.

title: Ethics Watchdog Urges Investigation Into Top Health Official, Alleging Conflict of Interest Over Hormone Therapy Policy
content:
A nonpartisan ethics watchdog group has asked for an investigation into whether a top Department of Health and Human Services official violated ethics laws after a recent ProPublica investigation revealed actions experts called “alarming” and an “obvious conflict of interest.” 

Alicia Jackson, who heads the Advanced Research Projects Agency for Health, publicly endorsed a change to federal health policy on hormone replacement therapies while owning stock in a company that provides access to menopause treatments. 

In a letter to the department’s inspector general, the Campaign Legal Center also questioned whether Jackson properly identified up to $400 million in underlying assets held by her husband’s investment firm. The center’s review identified an additional potential conflict — investments in a second firm that provides hormone treatments for menopause. 

Jackson, who heads the HHS agency that invests taxpayer money in medical technology and research, was recently placed on administrative leave, though health officials have not publicly explained why.

title: ‘You cannot build peace on a burning planet,’ UN chief tells Cop31 in farewell speech
content:
António Guterres says climate action central to every aspect of UN’s work, as leaders depart Cop31 and talks go on

Tackling the climate crisis is central to all of human life and must be at the forefront of global governance, the outgoing UN secretary general has said in an emotional farewell address at the Cop31 climate summit.

“You cannot build peace on a burning planet,” António Guterres said at his final climate press conference as secretary general on Friday. “You cannot eradicate poverty when climate disasters keep throwing people back into it. You cannot promise young people a better future while destroying the natural systems on which that future depends.”

title: Caregivers are the unsung heroes of climate resilience
content:
Science tells us that the world must act faster to limit global warming, which is largely driven by the burning of fossil fuels.

Bold climate action is essential for cutting greenhouse gas pollution, expanding renewable energy, and protecting communities and ecosystems.

Bold climate action is also essential for gender equality. As UN Women warns, the climate crisis is not gender-neutral – and neither is climate resilience, the strengthening of communities for the impacts of climate change.

As climate change intensifies, more communities, especially in climate hotspots and low-income and rural areas of the Global South, are suffering through stronger, longer-lasting disasters and instability.

And it is women and girls – their care work and often unpaid labour – that are left holding them together.

Care work in a warming world: Learn the what, why, and how of the climate-care nexus and what it means for women and girls.

The climate-care nexus refers to the many ways in which care work interacts with climate change, environmental degradation, and biodiversity loss.

title: Merikotkan paluu on suomalaisen luonnonsuojelun menestystarina
content:
Merikotka (Haliaeetus albicilla) oli aikoinaan harvinainen laji Euroopassa tarkoituksellisen tappamisen ja ympäristön saastumisen vuoksi. Sittemmin niiden määrät ovat lisääntyneet monilla alueilla sekä lainsäädännöllisen suojelun että puhtaampien elinympäristöjen ansiosta. 

Turun ja Helsingin yliopistojen sekä Sveitsin lintutieteellisen instituutin tutkijat ovat analysoineet yli 50 vuoden aikana kerättyä aineistoa Suomen Itämeren alueelta ja Lapista. Aineisto sisältää pesivien parien ja poikasten lukumäärät noin 2 500 pesästä, jotka sijaitsivat lähes 1 000 reviirillä, sekä yli 7 100 yksilön rengastustiedot, uudelleenhavainnot, kuolleiden yksilöiden löydöt ja geneettisen tunnistuksen. Asiasta kerrotaan Turun yliopiston tiedotteessa.

Kun kaikki aineistot yhdistettiin samaan populaatiomalliin, havaittiin molemmissa populaatioissa samankaltaista, noin yhdeksän prosentin vuosittaista kasvua. Kasvua tuki pitkäikäisille petolinnuille tyypillinen aikuisten korkea eloonjäämisaste. Populaatioiden välillä oli kuitenkin eroja eri ikäluokkien hengissä selviytymisessä.

title: Attacks on the Freedom of Assembly: Lessons from Digital Rights Defenders
content:
In 2026, two cases revealed how civic space is eroding, and those defending digital freedom and combating disinformation are on the frontline.

RightsCon, the world’s leading summit on human rights and technology, was due to be held in Lusaka, Zambia on May 5-8. Civil society, technologists, academics and policymakers were set to tackle some of the digital age’s most pressing issues: AI, surveillance, the militarisation of tech, disinformation, and online hate, among them.

But just days before the summit was going to open, and with more than 3,000 delegates about to arrive in Lusaka, the Zambian government unilaterally postponed the event because it did not align with “national values”. The decision, according to local reports, was made after Chinese diplomats pressured the Zambian government, objecting to the presence of Taiwanese civil society delegates at the conference.

In October, another attempt by a foreign power to intervene in a civil society gathering occurred.

title: Peace on Moscow’s terms: disinformation ahead of the Abu Dhabi talks
content:
On 10-11 November, Russia and Ukraine held US-mediated peace talks in Abu Dhabi. Before the meeting, the Kremlin had stated that it is genuinely ready for talks, yet its FIMI machine had been working overtime ahead of the negotiations, seeking to shape the talks before they even begun. By portraying Europe as an obstacle to peace, pushing to exclude it from the negotiating table, and presenting Moscow’s demands as non-negotiable, Russia tried to undermine Ukraine’s and Europe’s positions and maximise the concessions it can extract. For the Kremlin, disinformation is not just commentary on the peace process. It is part of its negotiating strategy.

Ahead of the peace talks in Abu Dhabi, Russia set out to argue that Europe should be kept out of the negotiations. Russian officials and pro-Kremlin commentators have been pushing the same message:

  • Kremlin spokesperson Dmitry Peskov insisted that the negotiations should involve only Russia, Ukraine, and the US as a mediator, arguing that European governments’ stance is ‘provocative’ and aimed at prolonging the war.
  • Foreign Ministry spokesperson Maria Zakharova declared that European countries have ‘no business’ being at the negotiating table.

title: Demokratiaa ilman poliitikkoja? Poliittisen osallistumisen ja toimijuuden solmukohtia
content:
Monet kokevat mahdollisuutensa vaikuttaa pieniksi tai jopa olemattomiksi. Pystyvätkö demokraattiset innovaatiot antamaan valtaa ja toimijuutta tavan kansalaisille?

Suomea on tavattu pitää monin tavoin esimerkkinä onnistuneesta demokraattisesta yhteiskunnasta. Vaalien jälkeen tehtävät eduskuntatutkimukset ovat kuitenkin jo pitkään kertoneet eri yhteiskunnallisten ryhmien osallistumisen eriarvoistumisesta.

Karkeasti ottaen osallistumiseen vaikuttavat varallisuus, koulutustaso, perhetausta ja yleinen hyvinvointi. Osallistuminen siis seuraa osallisuutta. Suomeen on syntynyt osattomuuden ja osallistumattomuuden taskuja, joissa yhteiskuntaan osallistuminen on jotain, minkä koetaan kuuluvan muille ihmisille.

Esimerkiksi sosiologi Lotta Junnilainen on teoksessaan Lähiökylä — Tutkimus yhteisöllisyydestä ja eriarvoisuudesta kuvaillut ilmapiiriä lähiöissä, jossa kaikki yhteiskunnallinen vaikuttaminen koetaan itselle vieraaksi. Tällaisiin kokemuksiin liittyy monesti tunne syrjään jätetyksi tulemisesta ja oman äänen puutteesta.

title: AI Now Statement on the Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act (BAAJA) to US Congress
content:
The AI Now Institute has released a statement outlining concerns with the Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act (BAAJA), which serves as a backdoor bailout of the AI industry. The statement’s key points are as follows:

  • BAAJA is a vote for a “backdoor bailout” of the AI industry.
  • BAAJA preempts the few levers that local, state, and Tribal authorities have to hold Big Tech accountable.
  • BAAJA supercharges AI data center expansion in exchange for token ratepayer protections.

    • Last week, voters across the country made their position clear by rejecting the AI buildout and electing representatives who are championing data center moratoria. Now, Congress has a choice to make: do the bidding of Silicon Valley and special interests or stand with local communities working to shape their own futures.

title: NATO: The Shift from Budgets to Battlefields
content:
The alliance’s next test will not be measured in percentages of GDP; it will be judged on its ability to defend its territory, defeat aggression, and sustain military operations against a capable adversary. 

For too long, discussions about NATO’s effectiveness have been dominated by spending. The argument has been politically useful, particularly in persuading European capitals to invest more, but it has obscured a more important question: what can NATO’s forces actually accomplish? 

It’s an important distinction. Spending is an input. Military capability is an output. Operational readiness determines whether it can be employed when needed. 

At the 2025 Hague Summit, NATO allies committed to investing 5% of GDP into defense and security by 2035. The commitment marked a substantial advance from the previous 2% benchmark, and by the July 2026 Ankara Summit, European members and Canada had increased defense investment by more than $139bn. 

Europe has underinvested in its defense for decades, so the commitments in the face of a deteriorating security environment matter, but NATO cannot afford to confuse financial progress with military effectiveness.

title: Documenting the Egungun Masorantan Festival in Igosun: Preserving Yoruba Living Heritage Through Community-Based Digital Documentation
content:
On Saturday, 22 August 2025, the African Institute for Heritage Intelligence (AIHI) in collaboration with Yoruba Wikipedia Fan Club Offa, documented the annual Egungun Masorantan Festival, also known as Egungun Onigosun, in Igosun, Oyun Local Government Area of Kwara State, Nigeria. The documentation team which was lead by Salako Lukman Olamilekan the documentation formed part of the Institute’s community heritage project, which seeks to preserve, document and improve access to African cultural heritage through digital technologies, open knowledge and community engagement.

The Egungun Masorantan is a distinctive traditional masquerade associated with the King of Igosun and represents an important expression of the town’s Yoruba cultural identity. Beyond its visual appearance and public performance, the masquerade embodies layers of indigenous knowledge, spirituality, oral history, traditional craftsmanship, music, ritual practices and community memory.

title: Berlin's big plan to evict its landlords
content: Tobi lives in a 50 sq metre apartment in Berlin-Neukölln. His landlord, the real estate company Deutsche Wohnen, thinks it has a storage room. It does not. Every two years, Deutsche Wohnen sends Tobi a letter announcing a rent increase, listing the storage room as a feature that has not yet been priced into his rent. Each time, Tobi refuses. “I respond that no, I still don’t have a storage room. Or they tell me that my bathroom tiles, which are plain white except for two small lines of red and orange square tiles, are a value-adding feature. Some things are really silly.” In 11 years, he’s turned down five increases. In the same block, Jen has had a leak above her kitchen for three years. “I’ve reported it eight times. Sometimes you get an inspection appointment, someone comes, looks at it, and then nothing happens. A year ago they did repair it, but after six months it came back.” Instead, Tobi said, “they build parking spaces and bike racks, because those are value-adding characteristics and let them charge everyone a little more rent.” Tobi and Jen are among the 53% of Germans who rent, more than in any other EU country. title: Pakistan: Human Rights Organizations Call for Release of Political Prisoner Idris Khattak
content:
On the seven-year anniversary of Idris Khattak’s detention in Pakistan, we, the undersigned organizations, call for his immediate and unconditional release. 

Idris Khattak is a well-known Pashtun human rights defender who spent decades documenting human rights abuses, including enforced disappearances, in Pakistan’s Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Province and the former Federally Administered Tribal Areas. On November 13, 2019, he was abducted and disappeared. For the next seven months, his family did not know whether he was alive or dead.

title: Young turtles find refuge in both natural and artificial wetlands in UAE – new study
content:
Coastal wetlands, such as mangroves and saltmarshes, are rapidly disappearing yet they are incredibly important for young turtles.

In a new study, my colleagues and I used satellite tags to track young green turtles in a protected wetland in Sharjah, UAE. Our results reveal just how important these remaining natural spaces are to young turtles.

But we also found that nature can find a way to thrive in unexpected, human-made environments too. So protecting these habitats and the connections between wetlands, artificial environments and the open sea is essential to ensuring wildlife can persist in an increasingly human-shaped world.

Coastal wetlands protect our shorelines from storms, store carbon and provide important nursery habitats for marine life. Yet scientists still know surprisingly little about how marine wildlife, including turtles, sharks and rays, use these environments. Knowing where these animals feed, shelter and move helps identify which areas need protection and whether existing protected areas are working.

title: "It's Just Barbarism": Dr. Feroze Sidhwa Mourns Friend Killed in Israeli Hospital Strike in Gaza
content:
Israel’s latest bombing of Nasser Hospital in Gaza on Thursday killed six Palestinians, including surgeon Dr. Rizk Abu Shaira. He was featured in the recent documentary American Doctor, which follows international medical volunteers in Gaza’s battered hospitals as they work alongside Palestinian colleagues.

Israel claimed, without providing evidence, that it targeted a senior Hamas militant in the hospital strike. Israel has repeatedly bombed medical facilities in Gaza since the start of the genocide in October 2023, even though such attacks are prohibited under international law.

“It’s just barbarism. I don’t know why we’re supporting this,” says Dr. Feroze Sidhwa, one of the titular American doctors in the documentary, who demands accountability for Israel’s actions and a change in U.S. policy toward the country. “That’s an American-made bomb dropped by an American-made airplane burning American-supplied jet fuel.”

title: Saeed Shakiba Sentenced to Five Years in Prison for Imitating Ali Khamenei’s Voice
content:
According to HRANA, Saeed Shakiba has been sentenced to imprisonment.

Under a verdict issued by Branch 28 of the Tehran Revolutionary Court, presided over by Judge Mohammadreza Amouzad, the blogger and satirist was sentenced to five years in prison on charges of “assembly and collusion against national security.” The verdict was communicated to him on Wednesday, November 11, 2026.

It is worth noting that Shakiba’s trial was held before the same court last week.

Saeed Shakiba, a blogger and satirist, was arrested in early October of this year following the publication of a satirical video in which he imitated the voice of Ayatollah Ali Khamenei, the second Supreme Leader of the Islamic Republic.

In connection with the case, Mizan News Agency, the Iranian judiciary’s official media outlet, had reported that judicial proceedings had been initiated against the blogger, without disclosing his identity. The outlet attributed the legal action to the publication of content it described as “insulting and offensive.”
snippet: According to HRANA, Saeed Shakiba has been sentenced to imprisonment.

title: Yritysrahoituksen kohdentuminen ja toteutunut käyttö
content:
Esitämme havaintojemme perusteella neljä suositusta yritysrahoitusjärjestelmän toimivuuden ja julkisen rahoituksen vaikuttavuuden parantamiseksi:

1. Kasvuyritysten pitkäjänteisen, riskinkantokykyisen oman pääoman ehtoisen rahoituksen saatavuutta tulee parantaa. Erityisesti nuoret, aineettomiin investointeihin nojaavat yritykset tarvitsevat sijoittajia, joilla on riittävästi pääomaa ja kykyä rahoittaa niitä myös useiden tappiollisten vuosien ajan. Mahdolliset julkiset pääomasijoitukset tulee kohdentaa osoitettuihin rahoituspuutteisiin yhdessä yksityisten sijoittajien kanssa.

2. Kasvuun tähtäävien avustusten nykyistä vahvempaa kohdentamista mikro- ja pienyrityksiin tulee kokeilla. Näissä yrityksissä julkisen rahoituksen määrä on vahvimmin yhteydessä kasvuun, mutta rahoitusta saa vain pieni osa yrityksistä. Kokeilussa tulee arvioida, synnyttääkö rahoitus uusia investointeja ja kasvua sekä lisääkö se yksityisen rahoituksen saatavuutta.

title: Helsingin yliopistoon UNESCO-professuuri edistämään nuorten tiedeosaamista kestävään tulevaisuuteen
content:
Maija Aksela has been appointed UNESCO Chair in STEM Literacy and Future Agency for Sustainability for the period 2027–2030, a role she will combine with her research. 

Through international collaboration, the Chair aims to foster young people’s participation, hope and science skills for a sustainable future, and encourage them to study STEM subjects: science, technology, engineering and mathematics. 

“Young people want to understand the major sustainability challenges of our time, but above all they want to understand the opportunities that science and innovation offer, and to help solve those challenges in the future,” says Professor Aksela. 

The Chair’s main research and development project will be the LUMA Stars programme, a multidisciplinary international collaboration involving seven other countries besides Finland. Young people taking part visit research groups, attend science camps and meet researchers at universities and companies. They also serve as science ambassadors to their peers, and plan the activities themselves. The programme also develops, together with young people, new models of continuous learning for teachers, as well as open digital learning environments.

title: Hungary Pledges to Ratify European Treaty to Protect Women from Violence
content:
On November 12, Hungary's Prime Minister Péter Magyar announced that his government intends to ratify the Council of Europe Convention on preventing and combatting violence against women and domestic violence, also known as “Istanbul Convention,” as part of a comprehensive package of measures seeking to strengthen protection and dignity of women and girls. It is a welcome and timely step.

In 2013, I interviewed 37-year-old Lívia from Budapest for Human Rights Watch’s report Unless Blood Flows which documented domestic violence in Hungary. She told me she had repeatedly called the police about her husband’s abuse and that the police even witnessed him beating her. Officers told her they could do nothing “unless blood flows.” Other women described similar responses, some telling me they had stopped calling for help.

The new government package would strengthen enforcement of restraining orders, make misuse of intimate images a distinct criminal offense, and provide special protections for victims and survivors of intimate partner violence in criminal proceedings.

title: Traficom muistuttaa kodin reitittimen ja älylaitteiden suojaamisesta
content:
Kylmäjärjestelmiin kohdistuneet kyberhyökkäykset muistuttavat laitteiden suojaamisen tärkeydestä. Traficom kehottaa huolehtimaan myös kotiverkon tietoturvasta.

Kodin reitittimen ja internetiin yhdistettyjen älylaitteiden puutteellinen suojaus voi avata rikolliselle pääsyn kotiverkkoon ja käyttäjän tietoihin. Liikenne- ja viestintävirasto Traficomin Kyberturvallisuuskeskus muistuttaa, että laitteiden päivityksistä ja vahvoista salasanoista huolehtiminen on tärkeää myös kotona.

”Kodin älylaitteiden tietoturvasta huolehtiminen ei vaadi erityistä teknistä osaamista. Jo oletussalasanojen vaihtaminen, ohjelmistojen päivittäminen ja tarpeettomien etäyhteyksien poistaminen käytöstä parantavat laitteiden turvallisuutta. Erityisen tärkeää on suojata kodin reititin, jonka kautta laitteet ovat yhteydessä internetiin", muistuttaa Traficomin Kyberturvallisuuskeskuksen tietoturva-asiantuntija Antti Nikkinen.

Älytelevisiot, valvontakamerat, robotti-imurit ja verkkoon yhdistetyt kodinkoneet ovat esimerkkejä kodin älylaitteista. Ne voivat olla yhteydessä internetiin kodin reitittimen kautta.

title: Buro Media Launches Database of Lukashenko’s Inner Circle
content:
OCCRP’s Belarusian member center Buro Media has launched Friday a new database, “Favorites,” documenting the wealth, assets, business interests, and connections of people close to Belarusian authoritarian leader Aleksandr Lukashenko.

The project currently features 20 profiles, including members of Lukashenko’s family, security officials, businessmen, and public figures. Buro plans to expand the database with additional names.

Each profile provides biographical information, details of business activities, and current and historical assets held by the individuals and their associates. The database also documents personal and professional connections, sanctions, criminal proceedings, and privileges granted through ties to Lukashenko, including preferential government loans, tax exemptions, state contracts, and exclusive import and export rights.

title: European Intellectual History Since Nietzsche: A Free Online Course from Yale
content:
Taught by historian Marci Shore, “European Intellectual History Since Nietzsche” surveys the story of modern thought, from the late 18th century to the late 20th.

Along the way, the course explores major trends in modern European thought: Marxism-Leninism, psychoanalysis, expressionism, structuralism, phenomenology, existentialism, anti-politics, and deconstruction. Intellectual figures covered in the course include Nietzsche, Lenin, Kafka, Freud, Husserl, de Beauvoir, Heidegger, Arendt, Adorno, Sartre, Girard, Foucault, Derrida, and Havel.

You can watch all 25 lectures above. Or find them on YouTube and Apple Podcasts. Explore the course handouts here.

title: Microsoft outage renews European calls to detox from US tech
content:
DUBLIN — Friday’s widespread outage of Microsoft products has sparked a new wave of calls for Europe to control its own digital infrastructure — especially with the uncertain future of artificial intelligence at stake.

“Only 20% of European digital services run on European infrastructure,” Mistral CEO Arthur Mensch said in remarks Friday after he addressed EU national leaders during their first-ever meeting on artificial intelligence in Dublin.

The money spent on foreign, U.S. or Chinese, technology “could be reinvested here, on infrastructure we control and [to] finance European research and development,” said the boss of Europe’s leading AI frontier lab.

Mensch didn’t specifically address the Microsoft outage, which lasted nearly 24 hours and affected millions of users in 74 countries. Still, the shutdown of key tools like Outlook email and Teams messaging impacted plenty of the tech and government leaders gathered in Dublin to chart Europe’s AI future.

title: Members of Georgia’s Election Board Have Been Coordinating With Cleta Mitchell’s Network
content:
In the run-up to the midterms, members of Georgia’s State Election Board and much of its professional staff were coordinating with an activist group led by Cleta Mitchell, the conservative attorney who worked with President Donald Trump to try to overturn his defeat in the 2020 election.

The board sets the swing state’s election rules, oversees the conduct of its election officials and investigates allegations of fraud. 

Recordings of private calls and events reviewed by ProPublica show current and former state board members working with the Election Integrity Network and allied organizations on shared priorities. Among them: advancing the use of a controversial, error-prone software tool known as ELLY to search voter rolls for purportedly suspicious voters. 

The state board’s current vice chair, Janelle King, and her predecessor, Janice Johnston, have both attended meetings of EIN or VoterGA, an aligned organization whose membership and goals significantly overlap with EIN. Johnston retired in June but still plays an active role in state election matters behind the scenes.

title: World is now in ‘age of electricity’, energy agency chief says
content:
Exclusive: Fossil fuels no longer dominant energy source, IEA leader says, as summit considers electrification pledge

The world has left behind the age of coal, oil and gas and is now firmly in “the age of electricity”, the world’s leading energy economist has said.

Fatih Birol, the executive director of the International Energy Agency (IEA), said more than twice as much electricity generation would be added to the global economy in the next decade than in the last, as countries scramble to secure their energy supplies against fossil fuel price volatility and supply shocks, such as the Iran war.

title: Dr. Mehmet Güllüoğlu
content:
Dr. Güllüoğlu is a senior diplomat and public health professional with two decades of leadership experience in humanitarian assistance, disaster management and international cooperation. He previously worked as Senior Adviser to the President of Türkiye. Before that, he served as Türkiye's Humanitarian Aid Coordinator for the Occupied Palestinian Territory (OPT) to oversee the coordination and monitoring of Türkiye's humanitarian activities in Gaza.

From 2021 to 2024, he served as Ambassador of Türkiye to the United Republic of Tanzania. Between 2017 and 2021, he headed Türkiye's Disaster and Emergency Management Authority, leading a nationwide structure of 81 provincial directorates, 11 response brigades, roughly 6,000 personnel, and 100,000 volunteers. In this role, he helped develop the national volunteer model that proved vital for disaster response and public awareness.

title: Blood in the Black Sea: What Can Turkey Do?
content:
The Black Sea is now the world’s most dangerous body of water. Hundreds of attacks on merchant vessels have left littoral neighbors wondering how to respond to an issue fraught with risk. Turkish, Bulgarian, and Romanian defense ministers met in Sofia on October 28 to discuss possible approaches.

From January to September, more than 570 ships were attacked in the Black Sea, with at least 40 sailors killed, according to the International Maritime Organization (IMO). The campaign has made the Black Sea the world’s most dangerous commercial shipping route, ahead of the Strait of Hormuz, where there have been 24 deaths since the start of the year.

The upsurge in violence has disrupted trade operations and increased security concerns, particularly for Turkey, which has critical energy assets in the basin and controls access to the sea under the Montreux Convention.

title: Microsoft has suffered a global outage. A tech expert explains what went wrong
content:
Microsoft has suffered a major global outage, bringing many of its widely used tools, including email and cloud storage, to a standstill.

According to outage tracking site DownDetector, some 130,000 people reported issues accessing Microsoft Outlook as of early Thursday afternoon US Eastern time (early Friday morning in Sydney). In a statement on X, the tech giant said it was “aggressively pursuing all pathways to reduce impact” and “restarting affected servers to return them to service”.

In an article for The Conversation last month, I explained how the whole internet is unlikely to go down but several services can become unavailable together when they rely on shared systems.

This outage shows precisely what happens when that shared infrastructure fails – and why we must prepare for digital outages in a similar way we do for natural disasters.

title: "Parasitic Technology": Could Jensen Huang/Nvidia Scandal Prompt Rethink About AI?
content:
Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang resigned Thursday after reports of multiple extramarital affairs, including with an employee and a Chinese businesswoman whom U.S. intelligence officials accuse of spying for Beijing. The company says Chief Financial Officer Colette Kress will serve as interim CEO as the board searches for a permanent replacement.

Nvidia’s computer chips are at the heart of the artificial intelligence boom, driving the company’s value above $4 trillion and making Huang one of the most influential business leaders in the world. His spectacular fall from the company he co-founded in 1993 comes as the U.S. stock market has become highly dependent on a handful of AI-related companies and amid intense competition between the United States and China over control of the technology, with access to Nvidia’s chips becoming a major point of contention between the two countries.

Tech critic Paris Marx notes that the AI industry’s “circular financing,” in which companies are both clients and investors for one another, has created systemic risk.

title: Report on the Execution of a Prisoner in Mati Kola Prison in Babol
content:
According to HRANA News Agency, citing Hyrcani news, a prisoner was executed in Mati Kola Prison in Babol.

The prisoner, who was hanged at dawn on Monday, November 9, 2026, has been identified as Hossein Momeni, 32, a resident of Babolsar.

According to the report, Momeni was arrested approximately three years and seven months ago on charges of murdering his wife in Babolsar. He was subsequently sentenced to death by a criminal court.

As of the time of this report, the execution has not been officially announced by prison authorities or other relevant institutions.

title: France: Sweeping Bill Threatens Peaceful Protest, Rights
content:
(Paris, November 12, 2026) – A draft law that passed in its first reading by the French Senate on October 27, 2026, contains measures that would severely undermine the rights to peaceful assembly and freedom of expression, and are incompatible with France’s human rights treaty obligations, Human Rights Watch said today. The so-called “vandals pay” bill is now pending review by the National Assembly.

“Penalizing people engaged in their right to peaceful protest is the wrong answer to tackling violent disorder in France,” said Eva Cossé, senior Europe researcher at Human Rights Watch. “Lawmakers in both houses should reject this problematic bill entirely.”

title: US Prosecutors Ask Judge to Allow Bribery Evidence in South American Drug Trafficking Case
content:
American prosecutors want to introduce examples of encrypted communications and alleged bribery of government officials as part of their case against accused South American drug baron Sebastián Marset.

In pretrial motions filed this week, the Justice Department argued the evidence is necessary to give jurors a full picture of Marset’s alleged global drug trafficking network ahead of a trial expected early next year.  

Prosecutors told District Judge Rossie Alston Jr. that the evidence will also show Marset engaged in a conspiracy to launder drug proceeds.

Marset was arrested in a pre-dawn raid in Santa Cruz, Bolivia, in March and expelled to the U.S. with the assistance of the U.S. Drug Enforcement Administration. He was initially charged with money laundering counts, but was later indicted on drug trafficking and narco-terrorism charges.

Marset’s lawyers argue that the initial charge of money laundering is invalid because it involved a single wire transfer between Portugal and China that did not involve the servers of a U.S. bank. They say Marset never trafficked drugs to the U.S., and the narco-terrorism groups were not designated as such at the time of his dealing with them.

title: EU institutions survive Microsoft outage unscathed
content:
BRUSSELS — The European Union institutions kept calm and carried on regulating on Friday, as many other parts of the world muttered at their computers over a massive digital outage at U.S. tech leader Microsoft.

The European Commission, Council of the EU and European Parliament were able to carry on business as usual, with systems remaining largely unaffected.

Microsoft’s global outage, which disrupted Outlook, Teams and Copilot started on Thursday, with internet traffic monitoring site Downdetector reporting issues in at least 74 countries. The tracker logged nearly 140,000 reports of Outlook problems at its peak.

Microsoft on Friday morning said recovery was still uneven. “At this time, we have no evidence of malicious activity associated with this incident. We will continue to treat this with urgency until full mitigation,” it said.

At the European Commission “the impact … is very limited and does not affect our operations,” spokesperson Thomas Regnier told POLITICO. He said the outage had a “minor impact on a limited number of applications, such as the slowness of SharePoint.” Outlook and Teams were “fully operational,” Regnier said.

content: What if you had to pick between your deeply held faith and the life of your child? That’s the gutting choice that faced Marshall Phillips, an Oregon dad who was born into the Followers of Christ, a sect whose creed bars medical treatment. When his 11-year-old son was stricken with a dire health crisis, Phillips became caught between his faith, his family and the state of Oregon, which had begun cracking down on faith-healing parents who don’t seek medical help for their minor children. A decade later, Phillips was pulled into another one of his church’s life-or-death dramas when he was asked to care for a newborn whose twin had died because her parents had refused to seek medical attention.
