title: Eurooppa – milloin täkki repeää?
content:
The Ulkopolitist ja Eurooppanuoret järjestivät syksyllä 2026 Eurooppa ja eurooppalaisuus -teemaisen kirjoituskilpailun 14-19 -vuotiaille nuorille. Justiina Peltonen sai kilpailussa kunniamaininnan.

Vuoristoja ja jokia, kuumia kesiä sekä kylmiä talvia. Taiteiden, tieteiden ja sotien  rikastama historia sekä lukuisia kulttuureja, jotka ovat eläneet rinta rinnan jo lukuisten vuosien ajan. Samalla kun etelässä kilistellään viinilaseja, pohjoisessa  selkä punoittaa saunavihdasta. Kaikki nämä toisistaan irralliset asiat kohtaavat kuitenkin yhdessä paikassa: Euroopassa. Alueella, jossa ääripäät löytävät toisensa  yli 700 miljoonan ihmisen kautta. Eurooppa on kokonaisuus, joka muistuttaa  erivärisistä ja -kokoisista tilkuista muodostuvaa tilkkutäkkiä. Olemme kietoutuneet  tiiviisti yhteen ja pitäneet yhteisömme lämpimänä jo pitkään. Viime vuosien aikana  ommel on kuitenkin päässyt rispaantumaan, ja ennen niin tiivis rakenne uhkaa nyt  revetä rikki kokonaan.

title: Prince Harry slams ‘lawless’ social media’s impact on children
content:
BRUSSELS — Royalty descended on the European Parliament on Tuesday as Prince Harry slammed Big Tech for creating a world of “chaos.”

“A handful of very powerful people … would like to see the world as a social media world: lawless, no consequence, complete chaos, division,” the Duke of Sussex said at an event on online safety for children.

Speaking in a room packed to the brim with journalists and photographers, Harry called for stricter rules on social media platforms to protect kids from content that could lead to suicide or self-harm.

He expressed reservations about the privacy policies of social media platforms, which he said bar parents from knowing how their children died. “That cannot be right,” a visibly upset Harry said.

His wife, Meghan Markle, was present but withdrew from an address on Tuesday’s panel.

The European Commission regulates online platforms through its Digital Services Act and is planning a special regime for minors under the Kids Act.

The burden of proof that platforms are safe should be on the companies rather than on parents, and “the EU Kids Act is exactly that,” said the prince, praising an EU proposal that would bar access to social media for under-13s.

The CDIF-4-XAS project addresses the critical challenge of data interoperability within X-ray Absorption Spectroscopy (XAS). While XAS is fundamental to diverse scientific fields ranging from physics to environmental science, the lack of standardized metadata and formats hinders the FAIR sharing of data across domains. Existing community standards like XDI and NeXus facilitate internal exchange but often lack the contextualization required for broader reuse. This document outlines the implementation of the Cross-Domain Interoperability Framework (CDIF) within the XAS domain to establish a lingua franca for FAIR data exchange.

title: Voters repudiated Trump. Grassroots momentum will shape what comes next.
content:
This article was originally published on Waging Nonviolence and Truthout.

The broad strokes of the midterms are clear: a massive repudiation of MAGA’s fascist wave has ended the Trump 2.0 era of congressional complicity with his authoritarian takeover. Trump’s lame duck presidency now begins. 

This lopsided electoral rejection is historically rare: Flipping control of both the House and Senate in a midterm has only occurred three times since World War II (1946, 1994 and 2006). The breakthroughs are astounding: the first Native American female governor and senator, five Black governors, the first majority of Democratic governors in 16 years, and critical downballot wins like the first Democrat to win as Texan oil regulator since 1990 and the first openly transgender state legislator in Alabama.

title: Commons Stories: Part 4
content:
The commons belongs to everyone and no one.

It is composed of the gifts of nature, including the coalescence of human creations. The knowledge commons is the amalgamation of our creative instincts, a shimmering web of art and discovery. Every work we make is superimposed atop those that came before it, using tools that our ancestors made possible. What a beautiful thing it is to make visible the gardens of our inner worlds, to witness those of others, and to care for them all together.

title: EU:n teknologinen suvereniteetti edellyttää korkean lisäarvon datakeskuksia ja kriittisten kyvykkyyksien strategista kehittämistä
content:
Euroopan datakeskuskapasiteettia kasvatettaessa etusijalle on asetettava korkean lisäarvon datakeskukset, jotka tuottavat selviä hyötyjä tutkimukselle, innovaatioille, työllisyydelle, kriisinkestävyydelle, kestävyydelle ja alueelliselle kehitykselle. Jatkuvia investointeja tarvitaan esimerkiksi European Open Science Cloud (EOSC) – ja Open Web Search -aloitteisiin, jotta Eurooppa pystyy säilyttämään ja luomaan arvoa Euroopassa syntyvästä datasta.

Pilvi- ja tekoälyekosysteemiin liittyvä tutkimus-, kehitys- ja käyttöönottotoiminta on sovitettava tiiviisti yhteen muiden EU:n rahoittamien tutkimus-, kehitys- ja innovaatiotoimien kanssa, erityisesti EuroHPC-yhteisyrityksen ja Chips-yhteisyrityksen kautta toteutettavien ohjelmien kanssa. Julkisen sektorin käyttämille pilvipalveluille ehdotettujen varmuustasojen osalta on tärkeää varmistaa, että ne ovat riittävän kunnianhimoisia vahvistaakseen konkreettisesti Euroopan teknologista suvereniteettia, mutta eivät samalla luo tarpeettomia esteitä uusille eurooppalaisille pilvipalveluntarjoajille.

title: Estonia’s secret to a digital state: Trust, technology and less bureaucracy
content:
Karolina Zbytniewska, FocusEurope.pl: In Poland, responsibility for justice and digital affairs is divided between different government departments. The justice system deals with the judiciary, courts and judges. You are responsible for both justice and digital affairs. Why did Estonia decide to bring these areas together?

Liisa-Li Pakosta: We changed this model in 2024, although preparations had begun earlier, when the government started working on artificial intelligence initiatives.

We quickly realised that, since technology now makes practically everything possible, many of the challenges we face are primarily legal in nature.

At the same time, we had fully digitalised our judicial system. In practice, this means that many of the legal issues we deal with are directly connected to the digital sphere. Bringing these two areas together was therefore a natural decision.

title: Europe's anti-abortion movement is rich and powerful
content: Six years after Poland's constitutional court imposed a near-total abortion ban on 22 October 2020, thousands of people took to the streets in Warsaw and over 20 other cities. “Women’s hell continues”, read one placard. Abortion is now legal in Poland only in cases of rape, incest, or when a pregnancy poses a threat to the woman's life or health, forcing many women to terminate their pregnancies secretly, or abroad. Today, protesters blame prime minister Donald Tusk’s government for failing to keep its promise to liberalise abortion laws after winning the 2023 election. Although parliament passed two bills in October to ease restrictions – described by activists as “breadcrumbs” – conservative President Karol Nawrocki is expected to veto them. Despite being home to one of the most restrictive abortion laws in Europe, Poland is not the only place where anti-abortion movements are putting reproductive rights at risk. A report by the Centre for Reproductive Rights found that over the past decade, Europe has seen an overall positive trend towards reforms improving access to abortion care. However, in some countries, outdated legal and policy barriers continue to block or delay access.

title: Ministeri Ville Tavion esitys hanketuesta on korjattava
content:
Fingo vetoaa muihin hallituspuolueisiin ministeri Ville Tavion linjauksen pyörtämiseksi. Somaliassa toimimista ei oltu ilmoitettu pois sulkevana kriteerinä hanketuen haussa.

Jaa

Ulkomaankauppa- ja kehitysministeri Ville Tavio (ps.) ilmoitti tänään sosiaalisessa mediassa, että ei myönnä hanketukea Somaliassa toteutettaville järjestöjen kehitysyhteistyöhankkeille.

”Ministeri Tavion tekemä linjaus on korjattava. Kysymme pääministeri Petteri Orpolta ja muiden hallituspuolueiden puheenjohtajilta: hyväksyttekö tällaisen toimintatavan?” tiedustelee Fingon vaikuttamistyön johtaja Ilmari Nalbantoglu.

Tavio toteaa Facebook-julkaisussaan, että kehitysyhteistyö Somaliaan on keskeytetty, koska maa ei ole tehnyt riittävästi palautusyhteistyötä. Suomi on keskeyttänyt maaohjelman Somalian kanssa kaksi vuotta sitten, mutta linjannut, että ehdollistaminen ei koske järjestöjä. Viime vuonna järjestöille myönnetyssä ohjelmatuessa Somaliassa toimivia ohjelmia ei suljettu ulos tuen piiristä.

Somaliaa ei oltu rajattu myöskään hanketuen hakukriteerien ulkopuolelle.

title: In Conversation with Vedran Horvat, Croatia
content: Vedran Horvat is sociologist, researcher, activist and ex-journalist from Croatia. Since 2015 he is the head and managing director of Zagreb based Institute for Political Ecology, educational and research organisation in the field of degrowth, climate justice, commons and municipalism. From 2005 to 2015 he was the director of Zagreb office of the Heinrich Böll Stiftung, German green political foundation. During last two decades he has been actively working on creating supportive conditions for development of green political project in Croatia, Western Balkans and across Europe. Since 2022 he is also associate of Amsterdam based Transnational Institute and GMF’s Marshall Memorial Fellow (2010). During past years he has also been in board of various national and European foundations or cultural organisations. He is editor and author of dozen of books and articles on green politics, climate change, commons and social movements. title: From a quiet life to the terror of armed gangs: The story of Haiti’s Kenscoff district
content:
On October 19, a unit of Salvadoran soldiers was also ambushed; the situation remains tense

Originally published on Global Voices

View of the hills from the road from Port-au-Prince to Kenscoff. Photo by Ketounette via Wikimedia Commons (CC BY-SA 3.0).

In the heights of Pétion-Ville, more than 1,500 metres above sea level, sits the municipality of Kenscoff. A rural area just 20 kilometres (12.4 miles) southeast of downtown Port-au-Prince, Kenscoff is an idyllic contradiction of sorts. Its breathtaking landscape is dominated by pine trees and mountain ridges, dotted with terraced gardens and agricultural fields that supply fruit, vegetables and flowers to Port-au-Prince markets, grocery chains and restaurants. Yet, because of its high elevation, it can also get very cold and foggy, with the sun often setting by five in the afternoon.

The majority of Kenscoff’s residents are peasant farmers, though some wealthy Haitians, craving more peace, quiet, and fresh air, have chosen to leave the nearby urban areas of Port-au-Prince and Pétion-Ville for the area’s pastoral charm and community spirit.

title: Miksi rikkaus kasaantuu yhä harvemmille?
content:
Se, että on yhä useampia miljardöörijengiin mukaan päässeitä, liittyy osittain teknologiayritysten läpimurtoon. Ne pystyvät hinnoittelemaan tuotannon itselleen hyvin kannattavaksi, eikä kilpailu syö nopeasti niiden innovaatioistaan saamaa hyötyä. Yhdysvallat ja myös Kiina ovat maita, joissa tämä ilmiö on poikkeuksellisen voimakas.

Monissa maissa myös poliittinen kehitys on suosinut sitä, että varakkaat pystyvät sijoittamaan tehokkaasti ilman veroseuraamuksia. Pääomien kansainvälinen liikkuvuus tarkoittaa, että on helppo siirtää varallisuutta paikkoihin, joissa verotus on kevyttä.

En näe varallisuuden lisääntymistä itsessään ongelmana, se on päinvastoin hyvinvoinnin kannalta hyvä. Suurin ongelma on varallisuuden kytkeytyminen poliittiseen vallankäyttöön ja normaalien demokraattisten prosessien kyseenalaistaminen. Superrikkaat käyttävät suhteetonta valtaa, mikä on ollut näkyvissä etenkin Donald Trumpin toisen kauden aikana. Oletan, että tähän syntyy jonkinlainen vastareaktio.

Dear INC Community,

As many of you already know, INC has undergone significant restructuring: we have no staff, no funding, no office space and is no longer part of an educational institution. We currently exist in the form of an independent research and publishing collective that loosely connects a distributed network of people. While this is a new phase in the life of INC, underscored by precarity and insecurity, we nonetheless approach critical theory, forward-thinking research, activism, and experimental publishing with the same spirit we had over the past two decades. title: Can Gadi Eisenkot turn the ‘disaster bloc’ into Israel’s next government?
content:
On Sunday, Israeli President Isaac Herzog announced he would grant Gadi Eisenkot – main challenger to Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu – the opportunity to form a new government in Israel.

It followed almost a fortnight of political gridlock, after what has been called the “most consequential election in Israel’s history” failed to produce a clear winner.

Eisenkot now has 28 days (with a possible 14-day extension) to attempt to convene a stable coalition government. He’ll have to bring together a deeply divided opposition.

Even if he succeeds, his government will face major challenges – including keeping his coalition together, a changing relationship with the United States, and escalating violence in the West Bank.

Read more: Israel election by the numbers: who might form the next government?

In Israeli elections, it is standard practice for the president to formally nominate who should bring a coalition government together. This does not have to be the leader of the party that has secured the most votes – in this case, Netanyahu.

Israel’s voting system is intrinsically geared toward producing coalition governments. The country has never had a one-party government.

title: Dad Asked 6-Year-Old Daughter if ‘She Had the Gun’ Before He Left Her in Line for Pokémon Cards
content:
Pokémon released its Mega Evolution Delta Region cards this week and one man in Charleston, South Carolina wanted them so badly that he left his 6-year-old daughter in line at Target at 1 am with a pillow and a blanket. 

According to the incident report obtained by 404 Media, the person next to the little girl in line heard the father ask if his daughter “had the gun” before he left her alone at Target for more than an hour. Later, the father told detectives he left his daughter behind so “he could maintain his place in line and avoid missing the opportunity to purchase the cards.”

Pokémon cards are big business and people will wait to go to wild lengths to secure them. Waiting in line outside of a store for days before a new release is routine. John-Michael Dooley was waiting in line outside of a Target in Charleston, South Carolina with his 6-year-old daughter on the morning of November 6 when he decided to run home. He didn’t want to lose his place in line so he left his daughter behind “sleeping on the concrete,” according to a record of 911 calls obtained by 404 Media.

title: Haiti: The governments of Haiti and El Salvador must ensure that the deployment of Salvadoran military personnel respects human rights
content:
Following clarification by Stéphane Dujarric, spokesperson for the United Nations Secretary-General, that the vast majority of Salvadoran military personnel recently deployed to Haiti are not part of the Gang Suppression Force (GSF), authorized by the UN Security Council, and therefore fall outside the mandate and monitoring mechanisms of the United Nations Support Office in Haiti (UNSOH), Ana Piquer, Amnesty International’s Americas Director, said:

“The Prime Minister of Haiti, Alix Didier Fils-Aimé, and the President of El Salvador, Nayib Bukele, must ensure that all operations conducted by Salvadoran forces in Haiti comply with international human rights law. The Haitian Prime Minister’s commitment not to tolerate violations must translate into effective safeguards. Both governments must make public the agreement governing the deployment and explain how they oversee the deployed forces, what rules govern the use of force, to whom they are accountable, and how people can report possible violations without fear of reprisals.”

title: Q&A: What is the Belém-Antalya mechanism for a ‘just transition’?
content:
• How has a ‘just transition’ featured in UN climate talks? 
  • Where did the ‘just transition mechanism’ come from? 
  • What role could the mechanism play in facilitating ‘just transitions’? 
  • What are the financial implications of the mechanism?
  • What is likely to happen in Antalya?

    • One of the key expected outcomes from the upcoming COP31 climate summit in Antalya, Turkey, is the launch of a “just transition mechanism”. 

    This follows years of calls from civil society to support a “just transition” as countries shift towards low-emissions energy systems and away from fossil fuels.

    At the COP30 UN climate talks last year in the Brazilian city of Belém parties agreed to establish a “mechanism” to support this goal, called the “Belém-Antalya mechanism” (BAM).

    Groups that have championed the BAM want it to act as a central hub on just transitions, providing support for workers and communities around the world.

    However, the details of exactly what the much-touted BAM will consist of remain vague, with developed and developing countries disagreeing about its functions and purpose.

title: Giving a voice to Europe’s mountain communities
content:
Europe’s mountains cover almost 40% of the continent and are home to 17% of its population. Yet many mountain communities remain on the margins, facing limited economic opportunities, depopulation and exclusion from decisions that shape their futures.

For four years, the COST Action ‘A European forum for revitalisation of marginalised mountain areas’ (MARGISTAR) brought together more than 200 scientists, policymakers and local stakeholders from over 30 countries to explore how these communities could overcome isolation and build more sustainable futures.

“It was a journey of discovery,” says Professor Juha Hiedanpää of the Natural Resources Institute Finland (Luke), Chair of MARGISTAR. “We explored the natural, environmental, social and economic relationships that shape marginalised mountain areas and worked together to imagine practical solutions for their communities.”

title: "A Crackdown on All Independent Voices": Egypt Shutters News Outlets, Prosecutes Editor Lina Attalah
content:
Lina Attalah, editor-in-chief of Egypt’s leading independent news outlet Mada Masr, faces a criminal trial this week on charges of “spreading false information,” just two weeks after being convicted of operating an unlicensed website and fined more than $50,000. A judge also ordered the publication to be shut down. The cases are part of a broader crackdown on independent Egyptian media under the government of President Abdel Fattah el-Sisi, including the arrest of the entire newsroom of another outlet, Matsadaash. More than 100 organizations, including Amnesty International, Human Rights Watch and the Committee to Protect Journalists, have condemned the arrests and prosecutions and called on Egyptian authorities to drop the charges.

“Putting us in jail is not going to solve the country’s problems,” Attalah told Democracy Now! in an interview Friday. “We need to be operating as journalists in our newsrooms as opposed to being defendants in courtrooms.”

Attalah says she and Mada Masr will appeal the ruling to shut them down, hoping to “use this crisis” as a way to fight censorship in Egypt and expand the space for independent reporting.

title: EOD4ECCCH kicks off at the Moravian Library in Brno
content:
TheeBooks-on-Demand (EOD) network gathered at the Moravian Library in Brno, Czechia, on the 8th–9th October 2026 for the first meeting of EOD4ECCCH, a new project supported through the ECHOES Cascading Grants Programme. The meeting explored how libraries can unlock the potential of digitised collections and connect them with the European Collaborative Cloud for Cultural Heritage (ECCCH).

Kick-off meeting participants

The EOD network brings together 35 libraries with millions of digitised pages spanning five centuries and several languages. EOD4ECCCH builds on this shared resource, shifting the focus from digitisation to the discovery, enrichment and reuse of digital texts for research, education and public engagement.

The project builds on two decades of experience in digitisation and optical character recognition (OCR), as well as the results of the Creative Europe-funded EODOPEN project in resolving copyright questions, creating accessible formats and involving communities. Its next step is to help libraries use the tools, knowledge and opportunities for cooperation offered by ECHOES and the Cultural Heritage Cloud.

title: We’re Asking an Appeals Court to Require a Warrant for ALPR Searches
content:
Today, along with the ACLU, EFF filed an amicus brief in the Sixth Circuit court of appeals in United States v. Sturdivant, a case where police warrantlessly tracked a suspect’s movements using Automated License Plate Reader (ALPR) data. Our brief details the vast, interconnected network of ALPRs that constantly track drivers around the country and argues that this tracking is a “search” under the meaning of the Fourth Amendment.

Sturdivant involves a series of robberies in and around Cleveland, Ohio. Using surveillance camera footage, police identified the make, model, and color of the robber’s car, but they did not know its license plate number. After running an open-ended search of two ALPR databases, Flock and ELSAG, officers learned a car belonging to the defendant had been tracked near sites of the robberies, eventually leading to his arrest. Faced with a motion to suppress the ALPR evidence, the district court held that Mr. Sturdivant had no reasonable expectation of privacy in his license plate number because it could be observed by members of the public, and that therefore he had no Fourth Amendment interest in not having his car tracked in public places.

title: ”Reilu peli, samat säännöt” – Suomen verojärjestelmä suosii ulkomaanmatkoja ja laivaristeilyjä kotimaisen matkailun ja ravintoloiden kustannuksella
content:
Nykyinen arvonlisäverotus ja yritystuet ohjaavat suomalaisten kulutusvalintoja pois kotimaisista palveluista, todetaan tänään julkaistussa Etlan tutkimuksessa. Ulkomaille matkustaminen ja ravintolamyynti Suomen merialueiden ulkopuolella ovat esimerkkejä palveluista, joihin ei sisälly arvonlisäveroa. Samaan aikaan kotimaassa matkustaminen ja Suomessa tapahtuva ravintolamyynti sisältävät veron. Varustamoille maksetun miehistötuen supistaminen sekä ylimääräisen matkustusveron käyttöönotto tasapuolistaisi kilpailua ja lisäisi julkisen sektorin tuloja. Taloudellisen tehokkuuden kannalta on myös ongelmallista, että verotus ohjaa kuluttajia markkinapalveluista kotityöhön. Siksi alennetut arvolisäverokannat kannattaa säilyttää palveluissa, joissa kotityöllä voidaan korvata markkinaehtoisia palveluita.

Hotelli- ja ravintola-alan verotus sekä yritystuet vaikuttavat merkittävästi kuluttajien arjen valintoihin ja toimialojen väliseen kilpailuasetelmaan. Hyvän verojärjestelmän keskeinen tavoite eli kilpailuneutraalisuus ei Suomessa kaikilta osin toimi eli verotus voi myös ohjata kysyntää ja tuotantoa pois taloudellisesti tehokkaista ratkaisuista erilaisen verorasituksen vuoksi.

title: Joint Statement – Cultural Deal for Europe partners call on the EU Council to reject the 30% cut to the AgoraEU programme
content:
The Cultural Deal for Europe is a trans-national, cross-sector partnership co-initiated by Culture Action Europe, Europa Nostra and the European Cultural Foundation

Ahead of the EU Economic and Financial Affairs Council of 10 November 2026, which will discuss the EU’s next budget (2028-2034), we, Culture Action Europe, Europa Nostra and the European Cultural Foundation – co-initiators of the Cultural Deal for Europe – call on the EU Council to reject the 30% cut to AgoraEU proposed by the Irish Presidency. Chopping €2.58 billion for culture, media, cultural heritage, and civil society – essential to Europe’s democratic resilience and hence the basis for our better future – would not only cause profound damage to an already heavily impacted culture (both arts and heritage) and media sectors but only save just 0.14% of the EU budget.

title: UN Report Highlights North Korea’s Deepening Repression
content:
United Nations Special Rapporteur Elizabeth Salmón addressed a UN General Assembly committee on October 27 following reports that North Korean authorities had increased the use of public executions, including for recent offenses.

In her report, Salmón characterized the government’s use of the death penalty as “a criminal sanction [and] means of social, political and ideological control,” alongside expanded surveillance and tightened restrictions on basic freedoms.

The report corroborates Human Rights Watch research documenting heightened ideological control since the start of Covid-19 and a recent Transitional Justice Working Group report that found death sentences in North Korea increased sharply since 2020, particularly for those accused of distributing foreign media in the country.

As the United States and South Korea pursue diplomatic dialogues with North Korean leader Kim Jong Un, the focus on security issues should not again displace North Korea’s many rights issues.

title: Tieteentekijöiden jäsenkysely: Tutkijat viihtyvät työssään, mutta epävarmuus kuormittaa
content:
Lähes kolme neljästä vastaajasta on tyytyväinen nykyiseen työpaikkaansa, ja 76 prosenttia kokee kuuluvansa työyhteisöönsä. Samalla yli puolet kokee oman työsuhteensa olevan tulevaisuudessa uhattuna.

Määräaikaiset työsuhteet, epävarmuus palvelussuhteen jatkumisesta sekä rahoituksen jatkuva hakeminen muodostavat haitallisen työstressin merkittävimmät lähteet tieteentekijöille. Lähes puolet vastaajista kokee usein tai lähes jatkuvasti haitallista stressiä siitä, että aikaa tutkimuksen tekemiselle on liian vähän.

– Tutkijat tekevät työtä, jolla rakennetaan Suomen tulevaa osaamista, sivistystä ja kilpailukykyä. Silti liian moni joutuu rakentamaan uraansa määräaikaisuuksien, apurahojen ja epävarman rahoituksen varassa. Pitkäjänteinen tutkimus tarvitsee tuekseen vakaat työolosuhteet, sanoo Tieteentekijöiden liiton puheenjohtaja Antti Pajala.

Tutkimustyötä tekeviä kuormittaa erityisesti rahoituksen hakeminen. Yli puolet vastaajista oli osallistunut vähintään yhteen rahoitushakuun vuoden aikana, ja joka neljäs oli käyttänyt hakemusten valmisteluun vähintään 145 tuntia.

title: MyTax will be down during the weekend – manage your taxes in good time
content:
The MyTax downtime begins on Friday, 13 November, at 16.30, and ends on Sunday, 15 November, at 18.00. During the downtime, you cannot log in to MyTax or manage your taxes there.

The Tax Administration advises the taxpayers to manage their taxes in good time before the downtime. For example, you cannot request a tax card during the downtime, nor pay your taxes.
“If you have taxes to pay, check the payment details in MyTax before the downtime and pay the taxes in your own e-bank,” says Joonas Jarva, Product Owner at the Tax Administration.

The reason for the downtime is an annual system update, during which usability improvements will be made and new functionalities added to MyTax.

“One of the most notable changes following the downtime is that you can submit annual information returns by acting on behalf of a company in MyTax. The change concerns annual information returns on dividends, timber trade and forestry insurance contributions, for example.”

Parties requesting tax-at-source refunds can do so in MyTax in future. Further, information on the first registration of new vehicles will be introduced into MyTax, where registered filers of car tax can use it.

title: Increasingly diverse representation in the Demos programme
content:
The group’s chair, Ella Turta, sees a positive trend in the growing number of projects seeking to tackle societal issues.

“We also see a growing need for co-creation and strengthening the resilience of civil society in order to reinforce its important role in impacting societal issues”, says Turta, who would like to see an even broader range of organisations from different sectors represented in next year’s application rounds.

The expert group recognises the challenges of the Nordic Region’s vast geography, including the practical difficulties of bringing people together across long distances. At the same time, the group stresses that Demos also supports cooperation in the Arctic Nordic region and projects addressing indigenous issues.

And: Bigger is not always better. According to the experts, there is also room in the programme for projects that are niche, unconventional or unexpected. The experts value applications that have a clear purpose and description of partnerships and expected results together with an innovative approach.

title: Ex-Belgrade Police Chief Denies Charges in 'Body in a Barrel' Case
content:
A former Belgrade police chief pleaded not guilty to charges stemming from a brazen gangland murder, while prosecutors have dropped the most severe allegations against him.

Former Police Chief Veselin Milić appeared Monday before the First Basic Court in Belgrade to deny charges of failing to report a crime and falsifying an official document, OCCRP’s Serbian member center KRIK reported.

In addition to those charges prosecutors had previously accused him of participating in covering up the physical traces of the May 12 murder of Aleksandar Nešović, whose body was discovered stuffed in a barrel that had been buried in the town of Inđija after a week-long search. Prosecutors have now withdrawn those allegations, while the investigator who built the case has been arrested on suspicion of illegally gathering evidence against Milić.

Milić was removed from his post as Belgrade's police chief, but he currently serves as an Assistant Director of Police.

title: Explore the Reading List for Harvard’s Humanities 10: The “Brutal” Humanities Class That’s Suddenly in High Demand
content: There are plenty of good reasons a student might want to go to Harvard. One is its long history, at least by American standards; another is the formidable accomplishments of the professors hired to teach there. But on some level, a teenager looking to come up in the world — or, in many cases, parents looking to put their teenager up in the world — understands full well that much of what an institution like Harvard offers comes down to its selectivity. Considering how few get in versus how many apply, it would be easy to believe that most of a student’s battle is won at the point of acceptance. Imagine the despair, then, of a newly arrived Harvardian facing another entrance exam and written application just to get a seat in Humanities 10.

title: AI-Powered Crisis Monitoring from Local Radio
content:
My first mission with MSF in 2004, Darfur, Sudan:

Every morning, the village elders sat by an old radio, completely still, completely focused. I asked what they were listening to. The answer: local radio stations reporting where incidents happened overnight, which roads were blocked, where it wasn’t safe to move. Radio wasn’t entertainment there – it was survival information.

That moment is at the root of what we’re building now at PeaceEye FlexCo: a system that gathers online FM radio content in real time, the team at Neptun Data Processing GmbH – neptun.ai cleans the audio, and separates spoken content from music and ads – turning it into structured early warnings for humanitarian and development actors, companies and local authorities alike, with the goal to improve their safety and security.

Grateful for the support of FFG Austrian Research Promotion Agency, and for our great partner Neptun Data Processing GmbH – neptun.ai, with whom we’re building this together.

title: Europe needs Nvidia. It’ll take more than a spy scandal to change that.
content:
BRUSSELS — Last month, Nvidia chief Jensen Huang got Europe’s full red-carpet treatment from the likes of King Charles, French President Emmanuel Macron and German Chancellor Friedrich Merz.

Now it’s crickets.

As an alleged Chinese spy scandal engulfs the man running the world’s dominant AI microchips producer, potentially awkward questions loom for European leaders in both the public and private sectors who rubbed shoulders and inked deals with Huang. But the silence also reflects the cold economic and strategic reality that Europe has no homegrown alternative to Nvidia.

A German government spokesperson said Monday in response to a barrage of questions on the upheaval at Nvidia that it “does not comment on the media reports,” and that “we always adhere to the highest standards, including when agreements are being reached.” A European Commission spokesperson also had no comment on the matter.

title: Watch: Where Do Our Generic Drugs Come From? We Dug to Find Out.
content:
These days, we know where almost everything comes from. Everyday items like food, clothes and pens all carry labels listing where things are grown, manufactured or even designed. 

So why is it so hard to find where prescription drugs are made?

That question set off a 14-month investigation into where our medications are made, how the FDA polices drug manufacturers and what happens when inspectors report issues inside factories.

The vast majority of prescriptions filled in the United States are for generic drugs, which are often far cheaper than brand-name alternatives. 

For years, Congress, doctors and watchdog groups have questioned the quality of generic drugs made overseas. India produces about half of all generics used in the U.S., but the labels on pill bottles often don’t list where a drug is manufactured. Inspection reports describe unsafe manufacturing conditions at generic drug factories, but the Food and Drug Administration redacts the names of the medications made in those factories. That means if drugs made in errant factories wind up in your medicine cabinet, you’d have no way of knowing.

title: Lainauskorvaus puhuttaa eduskunnassa
content:
Tekijöille kirjastolainaamisesta maksettavaan lainauskorvausmäärärahaan ei ole tehty pysyvää tasokorotusta kuluneen hallituskauden aikana, vaikka alv-kannan nostamisen vaikutukset tekijöiden korvauksiin pystyttiinkin kompensoimaan. Eri puolueiden kansanedustajat ovat kuitenkin kiinnittäneet huomioita korvaustason nostotarpeeseen. Sanaston laatiman ennusteen mukaan kirjallisuuden tekijöiden lainakohtainen senttimäärä uhkaa vuonna 2027 pudota 25 sentistä 23 senttiin, jos määrärahaan ei osoiteta pikaisesti lisärahoitusta. 

Syyskuussa edustaja Pia Viitanen (sd.) jätti hallitukselle kirjallisen kysymyksen lainauskorvausmäärärahan riittävyydestä ja kirjallisuuden tekijöiden korvaustason turvaamisesta. Viitanen kysyy, miksi hallitus ei ole ryhtynyt ajoissa toimenpiteisiin lainauskorvausmäärärahan korottamiseksi, vaikka eduskunta on edellyttänyt määrärahan korottamista jo vuonna 2021. Määrärahan riittämättömyys sekä kirjalainaamisen kasvava suosio ovat olleet hallituksen tiedossa useiden vuosien ajan. Lisäksi Viitanen kysyy, mihin toimenpiteisiin hallitus aikoo ryhtyä, että lainakohtainen senttimäärä ei tule laskemaan ja miten lainauskorvauksen riittävyys taataan pitkällä aikavälillä.

title: Which open source does Europe rely on? A survey for the EU Sovereign Tech Fund pilot
content:
The EU Sovereign Tech Fund pilot will make targeted investments in Europe’s critical open digital infrastructure. Whether you build, use, fund, or study open source, take the survey to inform the pilot’s design and investment priorities.

Europe’s digital economy depends on open source technologies. From operating systems and cloud infrastructure to cybersecurity and software development tools, they form the foundations of countless products, services and public systems. By some estimates, up to 90% of code in the digital economy is open source.

Yet the strategic importance of open source technologies is not always reflected in the resources available to maintain and develop them. The PHP2Shell incident in October 2026 underscored the consequences for European businesses, governments, and civil society when critical digital infrastructure is not adequately maintained.

title: Selvitys: Teknologia- ja digiministeriö voisi aloittaa toimintansa jo vuonna 2028
content:
Suomeen voitaisiin perustaa teknologia- ja digiministeriö jo vuoden 2028 alussa, ilmenee Teknologiateollisuuden tilaamasta oikeudellisesta selvityksestä. Uuden ministeriön perustaminen edellyttäisi enimmillään 30 lain ja asetuksen muuttamista, mutta perustuslakia ei tarvitsisi muuttaa.

Selvitystyötä johti entinen oikeuskansleri Tuomas Pöysti. Hänen mukaansa tarvittavat lakimuutokset koskisivat pääosin ministeriöiden tehtävien ja ohjausvastuiden siirtämistä, ja ne voitaisiin koota yhteen hallituksen esitykseen.

"Hyvin organisoituna lainvalmistelu kestäisi viitisen kuukautta, ja uusi ministeriö voisi aloittaa jo vuoden 2028 alussa", Pöysti sanoo.

Teknologiateollisuus esittää uuden ministeriön perustamista, koska teknologia-asioiden valmistelu ja poliittinen ohjaus jakaantuvat nykyisin usean ministeriön vastuulle.

"Emme esitä lisää hallintoa vaan nykyisen hallinnon kokoamista vaikuttavammaksi ja tehokkaammaksi kokonaisuudeksi. Tavoitteena on, että teknologiaa koskevat päätökset tukevat toisiaan ja Suomella on selkeä suunta", sanoo Teknologiateollisuuden teknologiajohtaja Sanna Malinen järjestön tiedotteessa.

title: Kysy politiikasta: Onko faktoista tullut politiikassa mielipiteitä?
content:
Kysy Politiikasta on juttusarjamme, jossa tutkija vastaa esitettyihin kysymyksiin.

Poliittisen julkisuuden kehitys on saanut monet kansalaiset huolestumaan totuuden asemasta politiikassa. Uutisten perusteella saattaa vaikuttaa siltä, että poliitikot voivat väittää mitä tahansa, eikä väitteiden osoittaminen virheelliseksi juurikaan vaikuta heidän kannatukseensa.

Ilmiö liittyy politiikan polarisoitumiseen, jossa erilaisiin arvopohjiin nojaavien poliittisten ryhmien keskusteluyhteys rapautuu ja kukin taho luo omat totuutensa, joihin uskoo. Yhdysvallat on ilmeinen esimerkki tällaisesta kehityksestä, mutta sama trendi on nähtävissä Suomessakin.

Suomessa on kuitenkin vallinnut vahva perinne puoluerajat ylittävästä korporatistisesta ja konsensuaalisesta yhteistyöstä: Päätöksiä on valmisteltu puolueiden ja järjestöjen yhteisissä työryhmissä ja komiteoissa, joissa on tavoiteltu kaikille osapuolille mahdollisimman hyviä kompromisseja. Virkakoneiston ja tutkimuslaitosten tuottama asiantuntijatieto on luonut päätöksenteolle yhteisesti hyväksytyn perustan, jota vasten erilaisia näkemyksiä on punnittu.

title: Europe is not building a defensive fortress, but only national sandcastles
content:
Europe has awakened to a new security reality. One of the main topics of a recent online debate among politicians and experts from Czechia and Poland was the question of whether the European Union is allocating sufficient resources to its defence and whether it is able to invest them effectively.

According to Czech MEP Jan Farský (EPP), Europe’s fundamental problem is not a lack of funding or technological potential, but rather the deep fragmentation of national markets and military procurement.

“Europe is not weak. It’s just fragmented. We are losing our potential in national disputes. We still plan, purchase and produce largely along national lines and outside EU,” he emphasized.

Data illustrates the fragmentation of European armies. While the United States operates only 30 types of weapon systems on its territory, EU member states use approximately 178. This situation has led to major complications for Europe in logistics, maintenance, training, and the supply of spare parts.

title: The strange appeal of Spain's useless bar napkins
content: Anyone who's been to Spain will recognise the little white napkins and dispensers found in its bars and restaurants. Try wiping your greasy fingers after eating a jamón croqueta or cleaning up a spilled caña, and you'll quickly discover they're pretty useless. You can easily get through half a dozen and still end up with dirty hands. These flimsy little things, known as servilletas, are an icon of traditional Spanish bar culture. In some places, a floor covered in them is apparently a good sign: it means the place is popular (although the habit has become less common as local authorities have cracked down on littering). But if they're so useless, why do Spanish bars keep using them? I decided to find out. Turns out I've been using them wrong all along. Servilletas are made from sulfite paper. It's not particularly absorbent, but it does resist grease. And that's the whole point. “They're useful because they really are a good barrier against liquids and sauces you can find in saucy sandwiches or saucy tapas,” Alberto García Moyano explained to me. García Moyano is a lawyer, but he also owns a bar in Barcelona and runs a blog about traditional bars across Spain, so he knows a thing

title: Freedom House Announces Laura Rosenberger as Executive Vice President
content:
WASHINGTON—Freedom House today announced that Laura Rosenberger has joined the organization as executive vice president. A widely respected and experienced democracy, foreign policy, and national security leader, Rosenberger will work with Freedom House CEO Jamie Fly to guide the organization as it expands its research, programming, and advocacy efforts during a period of strategic growth.

“Laura has spent her career confronting authoritarianism and championing democracy,” said Fly. “It is an honor to welcome her to our leadership team. Our Freedom in the World report has found that today just 21 percent of the world’s people live in countries rated Free, down from 46 percent two decades ago. Laura’s deep policy experience and work strengthening democratic resilience will be invaluable as Freedom House fights to reverse democratic decline.”

title: There is No Clean Nuclear Bunker Buster
content:

To be clear at the outset: there is no official indication whatsoever that such a strike is contemplated or authorized. President Trump has said he would not use a nuclear weapon against Iran, and the weapon he has named for any attack on the site, the GBU-43/B Massive Ordnance Air Blast bomb, is conventional.

title: Europe’s protest wave looks like 1968, but the demands are fundamentally different
content:
Spain’s November 11 general strike, called in response to a housing crisis, stagnant wages and rising living costs, is part of a much wider European story. Student-led protests in countries across the continent have spread from schools and universities into broad alliances with trade unions and housing campaigners.

France has seen large-scale unrest, initially linked to conditions in schools. German pupils have mobilised against conscription, thousands have marched in Greece over public education failures, and Serbia’s student protest movement has reshaped its national politics.

The obvious historical parallel is 1968. Then, as now, European student protests spread beyond campuses, crossed borders and drew workers into mass mobilisation. Politicians warned of social breakdown.

This comparison is not wrong. But focusing only on the similarities risks missing an important distinction between the two moments: that the grievances of the protesters are fundamentally different.

title: Paraguay’s bank collapse brought down a president – and exposed as myth the nation’s status as a ‘Dubai of South America’
content:
It started on Nov. 3, 2026, when millions of Paraguayans trying to access the Ueno banking app found they could no longer get their money. In a matter of days, the financial situation escalated into political crisis, in which the country’s president was ousted, placed under house arrest and charged with several corruption-related crimes.

The political and financial crisis exposes a central contradiction in Paraguay’s recent economic development. Ueno, a bank celebrated for expanding financial access to ordinary Paraguayans, grew through unusually close relationships with political elites and public institutions. And while the Ueno crisis came as a shock, there were clear warning signs.

content:
Ulkomaankauppa- ja kehitysministeri Ville Tavio matkustaa Antalyaan, Turkkiin 10.–12. marraskuuta. Ministeri Tavio osallistuu YK:n ilmastosopimusten osapuolikokouksen (COP31) yhteydessä järjestettäviin tapahtumiin ja avaa Suomen paviljongin. title: Bad news for kinky Brits
content:
Good Monday morning. Last week, the UK imposed one of the strictest, most vague (and therefore overly broad) new laws around pornography in recent memory. Recording yourself having consensual kinky sex in private could come with jail time, as could watching other people do it. And sex workers are the ones to feel the repercussions of bad laws like these first, of course, with many reporting content disappearing from their online stores en masse. Keep reading to learn more about what it covers, and how creators are responding.

“I adore breath play. I love being strangled, suffocated and drowned, and I love strangling and suffocating others. Interrupting oxygen supply produces the most intense sensation of euphoria. I enjoy it in my private life, and I offer it in sessions too.”

title: "Right Now My Vote Is No": L.A.'s DSA Rep.-Elect Gonzales-Torres on Backing Jeffries for House Speaker
content:
The next Congress will include about 100 new lawmakers in the House of Representatives, the largest freshman wave in decades. That also includes six newly elected members of the Democratic Socialists of America, bringing the total number of DSA members in Congress to eight. One of the incoming DSA congressmembers will be California’s Angela Gonzales-Torres, who worked two other jobs while campaigning and was massively outspent by her opponent, incumbent Democratic Congressmember Jimmy Gomez.

In her first national TV interview, Gonzales-Torres tells Democracy Now! she will prioritize immigrant justice, Medicare for All and fighting corruption, when she is sworn in. She also explains why she has not yet committed to supporting Hakeem Jeffries for House speaker.

“As of right now, my vote is no,” she says. “Over 100,000 Angelenos voted for courage. They voted for change.”

title: Why Fewer People Are Challenging Bad Patents
content:
The number of petitions being filed at the Patent Trial and Appeal Board (PTAB) has collapsed. That’s not reason for celebration. The PTAB is an important line of defense against low-quality software patents being used in lawsuits against people and companies.

The drop didn’t happen because suddenly patents have become higher quality. It’s simply because USPTO leadership is increasingly refusing to consider good challenges to patents, for reasons unrelated to the merits. The process has become so unreliable that many would-be patent challengers aren’t even trying.

Inter partes review (IPR) is a process that allows people to challenge patents at the Patent Office, rather than having to fight an expensive lawsuit in federal court. It’s one of the most important ways to get bad patents out of the system.

In the third quarter of 2026, July through September, only 97 IPR petitions were filed at the PTAB, compared to 327 petitions during the same period in 2025. Similarly, only 37 IPR petitions were filed in September 2026, compared to 129 petitions in December 2024—the last full month before the current USPTO leadership began reshaping how the Board handles patent challenges.

title: MinSkatt är stängt på veckoslutet – sköt skatteärenden i tid
content:
Driftsavbrottet i MinSkatt börjar fredagen den 13 november klockan 16.30 och slutar söndagen den 15 november klockan 18. Under avbrottet går det inte att logga in i MinSkatt och inte heller att sköta skatteärenden i tjänsten.

Skatteförvaltningen rekommenderar att kunderna sköter sina eventuella skatteärenden i god tid före driftsavbrottet. Det går exempelvis inte att göra ett skattekort eller betala skatter i MinSkatt under driftsavbrottet.
– Om det finns skatter att betala lönar det sig att hämta betalningsuppgifterna i MinSkatt innan avbrottet börjar och betala skatterna i den egna nätbanken, berättar produktägare Joonas Jarva från Skatteförvaltningen.

Driftsavbrottet beror på en årlig systemuppdatering. Under avbrottet görs det förbättringar i användbarheten i MinSkatt och nya funktioner läggs till.

En av de mest synliga förändringarna är att årsanmälningar efter avbrottet kan lämnas in också genom att sköta ärenden på ett företags vägnar i MinSkatt. Ändringen gäller exempelvis årsanmälningar om dividender, virkesförsäljningar och skogsförsäkringar, säger Jarva.

title: High-Profile Smuggling Raids in Hungary Point to Former PM's Brother
content:
Hungarian authorities arrested multiple suspects in coordinated human smuggling raids on Monday morning, an operation that local media and political figures say resulted in the detention of Áron Orbán, the younger brother of former Prime Minister Viktor Orbán.

The National Bureau of Investigation (NNI) and the National Asset Recovery and Asset Protection Office (NVVH) conducted simultaneous house searches across Budapest and Pest County. While police confirmed the multi-agency operation in a public statement, they did not immediately release the identities of those detained.

News outlet Kontroll.hu reported that the former premier's brother may have been among those arrested in connection with an NVVH probe into a visa facilitation network.

The reports prompted a public exchange between the former premier and current Prime Minister Péter Magyar.

Viktor Orbán indirectly confirmed his brother's arrest in a Facebook post, condemning the police action as a politically motivated "settling of scores" designed to distract from an "agent scandal" facing the current government.

title: “Don’t Try”: Charles Bukowski’s Concise Philosophy of Art and Life
content:
In 1994, Charles Bukowski was buried in a Los Angeles cemetery, beneath a simple gravestone. The stone memorializes the poet’s name. It recites his dates of birth and death, but adds the symbol of a boxer between the two, suggesting his life was a struggle. And it adds the very succinct epitaph, “Don’t Try.”

There you have it, Bukowski’s philosophy on art and life boiled down to two words. But what do they mean? Let’s look back at the epistolary record and find out.

In October 1963, Bukowski recounted in a letter to John William Corrington how someone once asked him, “What do you do? How do you write, create?” To which, he replied: “You don’t try. That’s very important: ‘not’ to try, either for Cadillacs, creation or immortality. You wait, and if nothing happens, you wait some more. It’s like a bug high on the wall. You wait for it to come to you. When it gets close enough you reach out, slap out and kill it. Or if you like its looks you make a pet out of it.”

So, the key to life and art, it’s all about persistence? Patience? Timing? Waiting for your moment? Yes, but not just that.

title: Visiting our Partners SOP Società Benefit (Save Our Planet)
content:
Good soil doesn’t make headlines, but it definitely should.. Last week I spent two days visiting four farms south of Milan with our Smart Farming partner SOP Società Benefit (Save Our Planet) – and what I saw there was truly exemplary.

Where SOP’s “Resonant” (R) line had been applied – via seed coating or through irrigation water – plant roots were visually 30% stronger and more resilient than without it. Thanks to SOP’s proprietary “SOP Inside” technology, Resonant stimulates activity in the rhizosphere microbiome, enhancing its synergy with plant roots. That helps plants access nutrients throughout every stage of growth and maturation, reducing the need for chemical fertilization, and with it, emissions of nitrous oxide (N₂O), a greenhouse gas roughly 300 times more potent than CO₂.

We saw this firsthand at the Cipolla, Dosso Pallavicino, Locatelli and Cascina Montonereo farms. At Montonereo, Mr. Prando, a highly experienced and enthusiastic agronomist, shared many insights with us as he treats more than 200 ha with SOP solutions.

title: Spain’s conservatives promise to relax climate rules if they win election
content:
MADRID — Spain’s center-right People’s Party has pledged to “put a stop to the imposition of unrealistic timelines” for climate goals if it wins the national elections on Nov. 29, a significant pivot from the Sánchez government’s pro-green policies.

The PP, the favorite to win the vote, said decarbonization is an “essential goal for Europe,” but promised to push for an “orderly, realistic, and fair transition,” according to the energy chapter of the party’s manifesto obtained by POLITICO’s Madrid Playbook.

The manifesto said it’s time “to reassess the pace of progress” in the clean energy transition “without dogmatism,” while conceding there are “environmental, geostrategic and economic reasons” behind the decarbonization strategy.

Spain under Socialist Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez has been one of the bloc’s most influential cheerleaders for ambitious climate goals, advocating to protect key EU policies like the Emissions Trading System, pollution reduction targets and the phase-out of gasoline cars.

But the PP’s manifesto shows that would change if the EU’s fourth-largest economy votes for a conservative government led by PP leader Alberto Núñez Feijóo.

title: Firm Linked to Trump’s Sons Got Nearly $40 Million in Federal Contracts to Screen for Ebola and Other Diseases
content:
The Trump administration awarded a small biosecurity company nearly $40 million to screen for Ebola and other infectious diseases just months after a firm linked to President Donald Trump’s elder sons invested in its parent company, according to records and interviews.

The contracts, one to screen for Ebola in several U.S. airports and the other to respond to disease outbreaks in the Democratic Republic of Congo, are seven times the total value of government contracts the company had directly received before. 

The company, XpresTest, has years of experience monitoring for COVID-19 and other diseases for the government at U.S. airports. That makes its parent, XWELL, an unusual hybrid, selling both spa treatments and biosecurity services. Last year, it made most of its money from waxing salons and airport spas that offer manicures, massages and “chakra beds.”

Huang built Nvidia as a family business but after the co-founder had an affair with an alleged Chinese spy, its board faces a difficult decision

For more than 30 years, Jensen Huang has been the seemingly unshakable public face of Nvidia. He co-founded the company as a young engineer in 1993 and oversaw its growth into a multitrillion dollar chipmaker and bellwether of the AI industry at large.

He’s also made it a family business. His children, Madison and Spencer, have taken leadership roles at the firm. While not a company executive, his wife, Lori Mills Huang, leads the family foundation which, as of 2024, controls over 60m Nvidia shares.

title: ‘A new age of climate extremes’: Earth accumulating heat at accelerating rate
content:
Increased heat will supercharge extreme weather events, warns UN agency as Cop31 climate summit begins

Heat is accumulating in Earth’s systems at an accelerating rate, the UN’s weather agency has reported as the Cop31 climate change summit begins in Turkey, with 2026 on track to be one of the four warmest years on record.

The imbalance between incoming energy from the sun and energy leaving Earth reached its highest level since monitoring began, the World Meteorological Organization (WMO) said in its State of the Global Climate update.

title: The dreamer who wants the world to read Nepali literature
content:
‘We no longer see Nepali literature as something confined by geographical boundaries.’

Originally published on Global Voices

Rishi Ram Adhikari delivering a speech at the Kitab Jatra Festival held in London in August 2026. Photo by Kushal Shrestha. Used with permission.

The Kitab Jatra Festival has quickly become one of the most vibrant platforms for celebrating Nepali literature, books and culture. The Festival is organised and hosted by the Kitab Yatra Foundation, a Nepal-based organisation promoting literature, reading, art and cultural exchange. Since its launch in 2018, the festival has grown from a local gathering into a dynamic international event, connecting readers and writers not only across Nepal but also in India, the UK, and the USA, with plans to expand to Dubai, Australia, Portugal, Belgium and Germany. Working in collaboration with various organisations and institutions, it has created a global stage where Nepali voices are shared, celebrated and amplified.

title: U.S. Supreme Court Deals Final Blow to Corporate Human Rights Accountability
content:
For the past two decades, the U.S. Supreme Court has been slowly weakening the Alien Tort Statute (ATS), a key human rights law that allows foreign nationals to sue persons or entities in civil court for harms resulting from violations of international law. The court’s recent ruling in Cisco Systems, Inc. v. Doe I dealt the law a final blow, foreclosing—absent new legislation by Congress—any future ability by plaintiffs to use the law to hold technology companies accountable for aiding and abetting human rights abuses. EFF filed multiple amicus briefs in the case, including most recently in the Supreme Court.

The ATS was passed by the very first Congress in 1789 and in just a few words gives U.S. federal courts jurisdiction to hear civil claims brought by foreign nationals against defendants who violated “the law of nations or a treaty of the United States." There has been a longstanding question about what counts as a valid civil claim under “the law of nations.”

title: OmaVero on kiinni viikonloppuna – hoida veroasiat ajoissa
content:
OmaVeron käyttökatko alkaa perjantaina 13.11. klo 16.30 ja päättyy sunnuntaina 15.11. klo 18. Katkon aikana OmaVeroon ei voi kirjautua eikä siellä voi hoitaa veroasioita.

Verohallinto suosittelee, että asiakkaat hoitavat mahdolliset veroasiansa hyvissä ajoin ennen käyttökatkoa. Esimerkiksi verokortin tekeminen tai verojen maksaminen ei onnistu OmaVerossa käyttökatkon aikana.
– Jos on veroja maksettavana, kannattaa hakea maksutiedot ennen katkon alkua OmaVerosta ja maksaa verot omassa verkkopankissa, sanoo tuoteomistaja Joonas Jarva Verohallinnosta.

Käyttökatkon taustalla on vuosittainen järjestelmäpäivitys, jonka aikana OmaVeroon tehdään käytettävyysparannuksia ja lisätään uusia toiminnallisuuksia.

Yksi näkyvimmistä muutoksista on se, että vuosi-ilmoituksia voi katkon jälkeen antaa myös asioimalla yrityksen puolesta OmaVerossa. Muutos koskee esimerkiksi osinkojen sekä puukaupan ja metsävakuutusten vuosi-ilmoituksia, Jarva sanoo.

Myös lähdeveron palautusta hakevien on jatkossa mahdollista asioida OmaVeron kautta. Uusien ajoneuvojen ensirekisteröintitiedot tuodaan saataville OmaVeroon, jossa rekisteröidyt autoveroilmoittajat voivat niitä hyödyntää.

title: From Vienna to Mogadishu – My Third Visit to Somalia
content:
Last week, I had the privilege of returning to Somalia for the third time – this time as CEO of PeaceEye FlexCo , together with Prof. Dr. Mutiu Busari from FUNAAB University, Nigeria – to kick off our joint climate-smart agriculture and Earth Observation initiative with SOS Children’s Villages in Somalia.

Every visit to this country leaves a mark. My first two came through my work with Médecins Sans Frontières (Switzerland) (2006) and SOS Children’s Villages International. This one felt different – not because the challenges are gone with more than 6 million people depending on humanitarian assistance, but because alongside the hardship, I witnessed something that left me with great hope: real, tangible change.

Baidoa – where soil tells a story At the Bonkay Climate-Smart Agriculture Centre, Prof. Busari and I conducted a comprehensive farm assessment to lay the technical groundwork for our Digital Soil Information System and IoT sensor deployment. We assessed soil conditions; mapped irrigation needs and discussed how Earth Observation data can support agricultural planning in one of the world’s most food-insecure regions.

title: AI pioneer Yoshua Bengio implores Europe to build frontier models
content:
BERLIN — Europe must build its own proprietary frontier models of artificial intelligence to avoid risks in relying on U.S. or Chinese models, world-leading AI developer Yoshua Bengio told POLITICO.

Working with open-weight AI models, built in China or elsewhere, would be a dangerous strategy for European companies and governments, locking in long-term economic and military dependence and multiplying cyberattacks, Bengio said.

The European Union is currently locked in a debate about whether to invest the billions necessary for homegrown frontier models, or to build applications on top of proprietary American or open-weight Chinese AI.

“Adapting models you don’t control and you may not have doesn’t work,” said the French-born Canadian computer scientist, who has been vocal in warning about the risks of the breakthrough technology that is largely based on the neural network systems he helped develop.

Asked whether that meant Europe needed to develop its own advanced models, Bengio’s answer was unequivocal: “Of course, because they are the key to everything.”

title: Lawyers in This State Are Allowed to Ghost Clients for Years. Why Don’t More Judges Stop Them?
content:
One morning in July 2025, I was the lone spectator in Judge Frank Palumbo’s courtroom in Philadelphia, watching prosecutors and public defenders haggle over the fates of defendants.

Palumbo paused the proceedings to talk to a lawyer he’d appointed to help a prisoner who had ineptly challenged his conviction. The lawyer profusely thanked the judge for the job. Then, Palumbo offered a bit of guidance: “I think I know where this is going to go. I don’t want to make it overly complicated. It’s real simple.” 

The judge said he’d pass along a brief that a different lawyer had filed arguing that there was no merit to the man’s claims in a related case. “I’m not saying plagiarize,” the judge said.

The attorney told the judge he got the message. “So it’s called a Finley letter,” he said, using the common legal term for that no-merit brief, in which an attorney can argue against the client’s claims and ask to withdraw from the case. 

“It’s looking like it’s going to be a Finley dismissal,” the judge agreed after a bit more discussion, “but every option is open.”

title: Ever dreamt of living in a castle?
content: The housing market has been bad for so long that I am ready to expand my horizons. But rather than turning to the usual suspects, like tiny homes or van life, I'm dreaming big: castles! Turns out there's more to them than I thought. Castles were originally built as fortified dwellings. Fancy homes for royalty and nobility without defensive fortifications are called palaces. And what about fortresses? Think castles built mostly for stationing soldiers – like knights. Of course, we shouldn't forget ruins, which for our purposes are rather uninhabitable. So far, my quest has led me to two insights. Castles dominate western Europe, while palaces are more common in the centre of the continent, and fortresses tend to cluster around historical frontiers. But, more importantly, with the state of natural gas prices, heating a castle would be a nightmare – and I hate being cold.

title: Beyond the beaches: The Dominican Republic and the global debate over deep-sea mining
content:
The challenge is not solely to declare new protected areas, but ensure they have effective management

Originally published on Global Voices

The stunning beauty of the Dominican Republic’s north coast at Los Haitises National Park. Photo by Jason Boldero on Flickr (CC BY 2.0).

When you think of the Dominican Republic, the first thing that might come to mind is paradise where sun, sand, and sea combine to offer unforgettable experiences to Dominican families and global travellers alike — but the country’s deep sea is also of critical importance.

Jonathan Delance, director of conservation of the National 30×30 Program of the Ministry of Environment and Natural Resources, says that Dominican marine ecosystems are one of the country’s “greatest natural and strategic riches” — diverse, highly connected, and fundamental to national life.

From an ecological standpoint, coral reefs, mangroves, seagrass beds, dunes, beaches, pelagic zones, and deep-sea ecosystems sustain biodiversity. From an economic and social standpoint, they are the foundation of tourism, fishing, and coastal protection.

title: ‘Rooting’ the commons: sharing lessons from Odisha, India and the South West of England
content:
A guest post by Amlan Mishra

A version of this post was presented at the ‘Law for the commons’ workshop at the Centre for Environmental Law and Sustainability (CELS), University of Bristol on 26 June, 2026 where several friends from Bristol Commons participated.

In this post, I hope to illuminate synergies between commons I study in Odisha, India and the commons we hope to grow in the city of Bristol – through commons movements in the city that I have been associated with. But what can I – a first-generation immigrant who moved to Bristol three years back – say about commons struggles in Bristol and the South West of England? All I can offer are some stories – some vignettes of my participation in these commons struggles. I hope to translate my PhD research which focuses on dispossession of forest commons in Odisha, India and use it as a vantage point to offer reflections from it.

title: Yes, the COP climate talks are far from perfect. But they still hold the power for change
content:
This week, around 80 world leaders – including Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese – will descend on the coastal Turkish city of Antalya for the annual United Nations climate summit, COP31. For the first time, the summit duties will be shared; Turkey will play host, while Australia leads negotiations.

At home, these national leaders have no shortage of issues to contend with: the challenges of AI, major wars and declining trust in democracy. Yet looming over all of them is the existential threat posed by a heating planet.

Climate change is a truly global challenge. Greenhouse gases have no respect for national boundaries, and the devastating impacts are being felt everywhere. We don’t have a world government, but we do have processes of international diplomacy to hammer out shared commitments. This is how the world is trying to deal with the climate crisis.

It can be easy to be pessimistic, but COP31 can still deliver real progress. In Antalya, countries will consider a global electrification target to hasten the shift from coal, oil and gas toward clean electricity.

If agreement can be found, this will be a major step forward.

title: COP31: World leaders must break fossil fuels’ grip on climate policy and people’s futures.
content:
World leaders at COP31 in Türkiye must stop backing the fossil fuel industry and start delivering the rapid, equitable phase-out that science, human rights and international law demand, Amnesty International said today.

“The world is not running out of climate warnings. It is running out of excuses. After more than 30 years of climate negotiations, governments can no longer hide behind promises of future action or avoid confronting their fossil fuel industry allies. The climate crisis is not a failure of knowledge, but a failure of political courage. It is time to break the stranglehold of corporate power over political decision-making and end the fossil fuel era before it ends us,” said Marta Schaaf, Programme Director for Climate, ESJ and Corporate Accountability at Amnesty International.

The climate crisis is not a failure of knowledge, but a failure of political courage.

Marta Schaaf, Programme Director for Climate, ESJ and Corporate Accountability at Amnesty International

title: The EU’s Industrial Accelerator Act and the Limits of Strategic Protection
content: The European Commission’s proposed Industrial Accelerator Act (IAA) marks a significant shift toward a more interventionist industrial policy. This Brief examines the IAA mechanisms intended to reduce Europe’s dependence on China in the battery and electric vehicle (EV) sectors (the IAA’s coverage of sectors such as cement and steel is not addressed). Although the objective of strengthening Europe’s industrial base is understandable, the proposed measures are unlikely to achieve that objective. Origin requirements and foreign investment screening are weakened by broad exemptions for free-trade partners, while thresholds based on price differentials between European and Chinese production are too low to incentivize private investment in Europe. By underestimating the scale of China’s competitive advantages and paying insufficient attention to global market conditions, the IAA risks raising prices within the EU without delivering meaningful strategic gains.

title: EU countries still can’t get it together on AI
content:
BRUSSELS — As European leaders prepare to project urgency at their first joint meeting on artificial intelligence, their governments are missing important AI safety and infrastructure targets.

The bloc’s 27 leaders are meeting Friday in Dublin to discuss how to accelerate efforts to stay safe and be more competitive on artificial intelligence.

Yet 16 capitals have missed a deadline to appoint a national authority to enforce the bloc’s AI safety law, and Brussels has also pushed back an effort to support the buildout of data centers because of national administrative delays.

European Parliament lawmaker Sergey Lagodinsky, a German member of the Greens, said the delays are undermining capitals’ credibility when speaking about Europe’s AI ambitions.

“Stop blaming the EU for missing the race if you miss your own deadlines,” he said. “Europe’s AI ambitions cannot be delivered if national capitals cannot get their act together.”

In a letter seen by POLITICO, Lagodinsky asked the European Commission to start a formal procedure against capitals for failing to meet their legal requirements under the AI law.

title: Tasavallan presidentti palkitsi 26 isää kunniamerkein valtakunnallisessa isänpäiväjuhlassa
content:
Tasavallan presidentti Alexander Stubb myönsi kasvatustyössä ansioituneille isille kunniamerkin Säätytalossa järjestetyssä valtakunnallisessa isänpäiväjuhlassa sunnuntaina 8. marraskuuta 2026.

Juhlassa luovutettiin 26 isälle Suomen Valkoisen Ruusun I luokan mitali kultaristein. Kunniamerkki on tunnustus isille, jotka ovat paitsi ansioituneet lasten ja nuorten esimerkillisinä kasvattajina, ovat myös antaneet tärkeää tukeaan yhteisöjen jäsenille ja osallistuneet yhteiskunnan rakentamiseen erilaisissa luottamustehtävissä. Ehdotuksia kunniamerkin saajista lupa- ja valvontavirastolle ovat voineet tehdä kunnat, seurakunnat, yhdistykset ja muut yhteisöt sekä perheen lapset.

Useilla palkituista on biologisten lasten lisäksi myös bonuslapsia. Joukossa on muun muassa sijaisvanhempia, yksinhuoltajia sekä Suomeen muuttaneita isiä, joista osa on ollut tukemassa maahan muuttaneiden kotoutumista. Palkittavien isien keski-ikä tänä vuonna on 63 vuotta. Iäkkäin palkittu on 94-vuotias ja nuorin 42-vuotias.

Puheenvuoron juhlassa pitivät sosiaali- ja terveysministeri Wille Rydman ja Väestöliiton toimitusjohtaja Tiina Ristikari. Lisäksi Vaskivuoren lukion kuoro esitti musiikkiesityksiä.

title: An 11-Day-Old Baby Couldn’t Stop Bleeding. For Hours, the ER Didn’t Provide a Critical Vitamin Shot.
content:
The emergency room was a mile from their Texas home. Stephanie and Eric Biesenbach took comfort in that when their newborn daughter, Gwen, wouldn’t stop bleeding from her belly button. They buckled Gwen into her car seat and made the drive over. 

Medical records from that warm August evening in 2023 described her condition as a “generic problem” of a bleeding umbilical cord stump. The doctor on duty, Nicole Malouf, had treated plenty of those as an emergency room specialist. She covered Gwen’s oozing belly button with a special gauze to stanch the flow, and when it appeared to stop, she sent Stephanie, Eric and Gwen on their way. 

They made it as far as the parking lot before they noticed Gwen had bled through her footed pajamas. Eric slid his arm under the car seat handle and lifted his 11-day-old daughter out of the car. They walked back toward the glaring lights of the Lonestar 24HR ER, a freestanding emergency department in New Braunfels next to a car wash, a McDonald’s and a deli.

title: It is time the government treated hunger and obesity as two interlinked problems | Letter
content:
The cabinet committee the MPs want should become the delivery arm of a statutory right to adequate food, writes Prof Kent Buse of the World Obesity Federation

Your report (UK government’s obesity plan ‘doomed to fail’, MPs warn, 30 October) arrives a fortnight after the Right to Food UK Commission asked the same prime minister for the same thing: a legal duty on government, a minister responsible for it, and an independent body reporting to parliament.

Each report sees half the problem. The Health and Social Care Committee wants prevention and treatment run as separate workstreams, and stops at urging ministers to stand up to the food industry. The commission sees hunger as a question of income and rights, but says little about the quality of the diet that low incomes buy. The same food system, and the same households, produce both hunger and obesity. Whitehall treats them as two problems, with two sets of ministers and no shared accountability, and so neither is solved.

title: How women bore the consequences of the First World War in British India
content:
Who do we forget on Remembrance Day?

For a long time, histories of the First World War have been popularly understood in a Euro-centric manner. But descendants of Indian soldiers and researchers have long pushed for recognition for the approximately 1.4 million men from current-day India, Pakistan and Bangladesh who helped wage the First World War for the British Empire.

Yet when it comes to the war’s impact on British India, many of us still think of contributions as military and masculine.

The double portrait of two Sikh risaldars, Jagat Singh and Man Singh, currently on display at the Art Gallery of Ontario is a testament to such recognition.

The men hailed from Punjab, the hub of military recruitment known as the “sword arm” of the Raj.

The piece was painted in London by Phillip de László two months before the Battle of the Somme in 1916, when many Indian soldiers were wounded or lost their lives.
snippet: Who do we forget on Remembrance Day?

title: How people in Montenegro are making their country cleaner
content:
And helping to make the goals for EU accession plausible 

Originally published on Global Voices

Screenshot from the EkoMapa website of the EkoGard organization in Montenegro. Fair use.

This interview is part of a series of spotlights on the work of some of the grantees of the Digital Spark granting scheme, as part of the Regional Support Mechanism EECA project, implemented by the Metamorphosis Foundation and TechSoup, in partnership with CIVICUS and under the Digital Democracy Initiative (DDI) that covers the Global South. It is being published on Global Voices as part of a content-sharing agreement. 

Montenegro is on its way to joining the EU; at the moment, the goal is to do so by 2028. The United Nations Economic Commission for Europe (UNECE) review in 2025 states that the country has made significant progress in aligning its environmental legal and regulatory framework, as well as much of its national legislation, with European Union (EU) directives. 

However, some problems remain, including waste management and a very low recycling rate —  less than 2 percent, far below the EU’s 50 percent target.

title: ESSAY: The Illusion of Decentralization: Cryptocurrency and the Contradictions of Digital Capitalism
content:
By Sam Ben-Meir*

NEW YORK | 7 November 2026 (IDN) — In a sophisticated cyberattack whose most intensive phase lasted approximately twenty minutes, hackers stole an estimated $6.3 billion in cryptocurrency from Binance, the world’s largest cryptocurrency exchange, in what investigators have described as the biggest digital asset theft in history.

The attack, whose precise mechanism remains under investigation, involved multiple points of breach and allowed hackers to transfer billions of dollars in digital assets into wallets under their control. Blockchain investigators have attributed the operation with high confidence to a North Korean hacking organization, although the investigation remains ongoing. Binance temporarily suspended withdrawals, pledged to cover customer losses, and coordinated with other cryptocurrency companies to freeze approximately $2.85 billion in affected assets.

title: Paraguayan President Impeached and Arrested Amid Financial Meltdown and Mass Protests
content:
Paraguayan President Santiago Peña has been impeached and arrested amid a financial crisis that triggered mass protests, and turned his own Colorado party against him.

The crisis was sparked by a major digital bank being ordered into insolvency earlier in the week. Peña previously had shares in the holding company that owned the digital lender, Ueno Bank. Peña has denied allegations that he helped protect Ueno from scrutiny.

In addition to holding public funds, Ueno banked millions of private citizens who have now been left without access to their accounts. 

In a Thursday statement announcing his resignation, posted to Facebook, Peña said his “greatest wish” was that funds would be returned to Ueno customers. He said he was resigning in order to "bring calm to the population."

By that time, the streets of downtown Asunción, the nation's capital, were teeming with protesters. In the Chamber of Deputies, both his allies and opponents rejected Peña’s resignation, and instead proceeded with an impeachment process. 

The matter then fell to senators who held an extraordinary session on Friday. Peña did not appear in person for his defense in the Senate, though he sent his lawyer, Ricardo Preda.
